title: feat(UX): define canvas overlay zones and layer ownership
body:
Closes #412 when exact-head evidence is accepted.

## Scope

- define the documented canvas overlay-zone contract for top/bottom corners, center, selection and tool chrome;
- extend the canonical `shell-tokens.css` layer scale with workspace-overlay `95` and accessibility `98` between Context HUD `90` and modal backdrop `100`;
- pin the complete named layer order in the global layer guard;
- migrate `WorkspaceSheet` off raw z5;
- migrate tab and phone More menus off raw z6 to the canonical popover tier;
- move floating workspace panels/tablet drawers onto the workspace-overlay tier without changing panel behavior;
- preserve canvas pointer ownership with pointer-transparent zone hosts and opt-in interactive child bounds;
- add deterministic contract tests and stable overlay-role attributes for browser evidence.

## Exact integration base

`main` @ `4184551be3e75636d7feea93fda13699b00b4b43`.

Current branch is directly ahead of that head with no behind commits.

## Ownership boundary

PR #361 is still open and owns `apps/web/src/App.tsx`. This PR does not mutate `App.tsx`. The known transformed command-palette wrapper there remains an explicit external exception until #361 releases the host path.

No CAD hit testing, snapping, camera semantics, project persistence or broad shell redesign is changed.

## Canonical layer order

- raised shell: 10
- Context HUD / selection/tool chrome: 90
- workspace overlays: 95
- accessibility escape surface: 98
- modal backdrop: 100
- modal surface: 110
- popover: 120
- toast: 200

All named numeric values live in `packages/design-system/src/shell/shell-tokens.css`. Workspace CSS only consumes those names.

This makes a drawer/sheet occlude HUD chrome only where it physically covers the canvas, keeps the skip link above ordinary workspace overlays, and still leaves modal infrastructure authoritative.

## Pointer contract

`CanvasOverlayZone` hosts are always pointer-transparent. Real controls opt back in only at their bounds using `arq-canvas-overlay-control`. Full-canvas transparent hit surfaces are not introduced.

The existing wall Context HUD remains a conforming independent implementation: pointer-transparent HUD host, interactive numeric field, and browser evidence for wheel/canvas ownership.

## Evidence

`packages/design-system/src/workspace/overlay-zone-contract.test.ts` locks zone names, reserved future roles, layer ordering, pointer transparency, canonical token ownership and removal of raw sheet/menu z-index values. `packages/design-system/src/shell/layer-contract.test.ts` pins the complete global layer scale and rejects future raw escalation.

Repository-wide `format:check` has an existing seven-file documentation baseline. #412-owned files must not appear in that warning list. Final exact-head unit, Engineering Gate and Chromium evidence will be recorded on #412 before closure.

title: [PUBLIC SITE V2] Implement ARQ editorial public-site system, starting with shared foundation and PUB-001
body:
Parent design-production gap: #205
Related UI/UX programme: #377
Recurring CTO reconciliation: #369
Repository authority: #332

```yaml

phase: W0-W6

reversibility: reversible
branch: codex/arq-public-site-editorial-v1
base_head: df04288c182bdfcee91f92e70b0e5d0017fc0628
owner: ChatGPT implementation lane
```

## User outcome
Turn the current static ARQ public site into a distinctive editorial-technical system without weakening its strongest properties: static HTML, no client-side JavaScript, no third-party requests, governed claims, accessibility, dark appearance, 320px support and 200% zoom.

## Current evidence / known gap
The current `apps/marketing` implementation is structurally sound but visually repetitive. It relies on one 68rem measure, a conventional hero scale and a small shared component vocabulary. `design/page-renderings/PAGE-RENDERINGS-MANIFEST.csv` still marks public visual assets as deferred. Marketing CSS also duplicates canonical brand colour values and currently uses a different dark green than `design/tokens/brand.v4.css`. `layout.ts` hardcodes a stale `REV B · 2026-08` footer label.

## First implementation slice
1. Preserve the current integration authority from #332. Do not assume `main`.
2. Add the approved master public-site plan to the repository.
3. Establish a canonical brand-token bridge for marketing without creating a second brand authority.
4. Remove the stale hand-maintained revision month.
5. Add an additive editorial CSS layer rather than destabilising the existing stylesheet in one large rewrite.
6. Add typed shared editorial primitives needed for PUB-001.
7. Recompose PUB-001 using governed current copy and explicit current/limit state pairs.
8. Preserve all public-site route, language, claim, accessibility and no-external-resource invariants.
9. Open a PR and use CI as the executable evidence layer available to this lane.

## Owned files for this slice
Primary ownership:
- `docs/design/ARQ-PUBLIC-WEBSITE-EDITORIAL-SYSTEM-MASTER-PLAN-v1.0.md`
- `apps/marketing/src/layout.ts`
- `apps/marketing/src/build.ts`
- `apps/marketing/src/editorial.css` (new)
- `apps/marketing/src/components.ts`
- `apps/marketing/src/content/home.ts`
- focused public-site tests only if required by the implementation

Do not overlap another active lane touching these files without reconciliation.

## Non-negotiables
- no framework rewrite;
- no client JS dependency for core content;
- no external resources;
- no fake product screenshots, metrics or capability;
- no weakening ARQ Language System 4.1;
- no second semantic capability vocabulary;
- `.arq opens` must stay adjacent to `does not save back`;
- 3D viewing must not become 3D authoring by implication;
- state cannot rely on colour alone;
- mobile/200% zoom/accessibility outrank exact visual mimicry;
- do not change the public route contract as part of styling work.

## Evidence required before completion
- exact branch head;
- CI/build/type/test status on that head;
- public-site language/claim checks;
- no-external-resource checks;
- responsive/zoom/visual evidence where current tooling can produce it;
- explicit report of any evidence that remains not-inspected rather than treating it as green.

## Completion boundary
This issue is not the entire 17-page rollout. The first closeable checkpoint is a verified shared foundation plus PUB-001 visual proof. PUB-002 onward should proceed only after that system is proven and reviewed.

```yaml
evidence: [failure-injection, browser-matrix, capability-fallback]
```

## 1. User outcome
If 3D cannot initialise, the GPU/context fails, or a browser falls outside the supported renderer envelope, ARQ keeps the project usable and explains what failed instead of showing a black/blank canvas or crashing the whole workspace.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
ARQ's 3D surface is real WebGL2 and browser/platform support is being formalised by #358/#360. The UI/UX programme needs deterministic renderer failure/fallback states comparable in trust to file/persistence failures.

## 3. In scope
Identify renderer initialisation/capability failure classes already detectable; add 3D loading timeout, unsupported-capability, context-lost/runtime render error and recover/retry/reload guidance where technically valid; preserve Plan/browser/inspector usability; allow return to Plan; keep current project/selection safe; provide privacy-safe diagnostics hook. If a lower-quality supported render mode already exists, expose it honestly rather than inventing one here.

## 4. Out of scope
No WebGPU migration, no new renderer backend, no pretending unsupported hardware is supported, no hiding repeated GPU failure behind infinite retries.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
Coordinate ModelCanvas/renderer owners and #358/#360 support policy. Do not alter semantic project state to recover renderer errors.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
Renderer failure never changes canonical project data. Renderer/cache state remains disposable and rebuildable.

## 7. UI/UX states
Deferred 3D loading, slow init, unsupported WebGL/capability, context lost, runtime renderer error, retrying, recovered, permanent fallback to Plan and browser/device unsupported.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
Project durability continues independently. Renderer failure cannot trigger false recovery/save messages or discard edits.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
Diagnostics redact GPU/browser details only as required by privacy policy and never include project geometry/content by default.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
Failure panel/status is keyboard and screen-reader accessible, returns focus safely to a usable surface and does not rely on canvas-only text.

## 11. Performance impact
Detection/recovery adds negligible hot-path overhead; no high-frequency polling. Retry attempts are bounded.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
Capability/init failure injection, context-lost simulation where possible, renderer exception boundary, Plan usability during failure, retry/recovery, browser matrix and zero project mutation/durability regression.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- blank/black 3D failures become explicit actionable states;
- Plan/project browsing remains usable when 3D fails;
- renderer failure cannot corrupt or mutate project data;
- retries are bounded and honest;
- support claims follow #358/#360 evidence rather than optimistic fallback.

## 14. Agent progress updates
Post detectable failure classes, recovery path per class, tested browser/GPU environments, diagnostics fields and exact evidence.

## 15. ZEUS CTO reconciliation notes
#369 includes renderer failure smoke after 3D changes and treats project-level crashes from 3D failure as a high-priority integration defect.

After an Agent interaction, the architect can answer what was requested, which proposal was reviewed, which revision it targeted, whether it was approved/rejected, what operation group actually ran and how to locate the result, without mistaking this evidence view for another project-history authority.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap

title: [UX-7.5] Surface Agent transport failures, interrupted runs and partial-outcome truth safely
body:
Parent epic: #392
Depends on: #421, #424, #418, #477

```yaml
phase: UX-7

risk: deep
parallel_safe: yes
ownership: [Agent UI, Review Centre result/error states, packages/design-system/**]
evidence: [failure-injection, Agent-evals, browser-agent-failure]
```

## 1. User outcome
If an Agent request fails, the user never sees unexplained silence. ARQ states what failed, whether anything changed, whether the proposal remains valid, and what retry/recovery action is safe.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
Pascal's open-source implementation illustrates a dangerous trust failure class: a stream may fail while users cannot tell whether earlier tool calls changed anything. ARQ's architecture intends stronger atomic governed mutation through #424, but transport/read-only/proposal stages can still fail and must present exact outcome truth.

## 3. In scope
Define a failure taxonomy mapped from real Agent/transport/apply states: cancelled, offline, timeout, provider/tool error, grant expired/revoked, stale project/revision, proposal generation interrupted, apply refused before commit, atomic apply failure, persistence failure after operation contract reports it, and any explicitly supported partial outcome. Show retry only when semantically safe; bind retry to the right project/revision or require re-review when context changed. Preserve any successful read-only result/proposal data that remains valid.

## 4. Out of scope
No generic `Something went wrong` catch-all as the only UI, no automatic regenerate-and-apply, no claim of partial application when the canonical apply contract is atomic, and no swallowing technical diagnostics needed for support logs.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
Consume actual error/result contracts from #421/#424. Coordinate #428 eval taxonomy. Do not infer mutation outcome from visible canvas changes.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
Mutation outcome comes only from canonical apply/operation/persistence result. The UI cannot guess that `nothing changed` or `some changes applied` from Agent prose or renderer state.

## 7. UI/UX states
Cancelled, offline, timeout, stream interrupted before proposal, proposal incomplete, stale, permission failure, apply refused/no mutation, apply failed atomically/no mutation, persistence/commit result as defined by canonical contract, safe retry, retry requires new review and terminal failure.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
If a canonical operation was acknowledged but persistence later failed, show the exact durability state from #459/#460 and recovery action. Never collapse mutation and persistence failure into one ambiguous banner.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
User-facing errors redact secrets/provider internals; support diagnostics keep privacy-safe error codes/provenance only. Retry cannot reuse stale grants across project/revision boundaries.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
Failure/status announced, retry/cancel keyboard reachable, no colour-only severity, focus moves to the error/result action without trapping the user.

## 11. Performance impact
No aggressive retry loops. Backoff/network logic remains with Agent transport owner; UI avoids duplicate timers/subscriptions.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
Inject each real failure class, verify exact mutation/durability outcome, stale retry behaviour, project-switch isolation, accessibility, and integrate relevant #428 red-team/eval fixtures.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- Agent failure never results in silent thread/UI state;
- user can tell whether canonical project state changed;
- retry is offered only when safe and context-valid;
- durability failures use canonical project state model;
- atomic apply failures are never misrepresented as partial mutation;
- diagnostics remain privacy-safe.

## 14. Agent progress updates
Post error taxonomy, canonical outcome source for each case, retry policy, injected evidence and any unrepresentable backend ambiguity that needs a contract fix.

## 15. ZEUS CTO reconciliation notes
#369 checks Agent failure UX against #424 atomicity and #459 durability after each Agent contract change.

title: [UX-7.3] Highlight and preview Agent-affected objects across Plan, 3D and documents
body:
Parent epic: #392
Depends on: #422, #425, #389, #478
Parent programme: #377

```yaml
phase: UX-7
lifecycle: blocked
blocked_by: [422,425,389,478]
risk: high
parallel_safe: limited
ownership: [Plan/3D/document highlight adapters, packages/workspace/**, Review Centre UI]
evidence: [cross-surface-tests, proposal-fixtures, browser-review]
```

## 1. User outcome
When reviewing an Agent proposal, the architect can see exactly which existing or proposed objects and documents are affected without confusing preview state with committed project state.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
#422 identifies affected semantic/document IDs and #389 owns canonical cross-surface invalidation. The Review Centre needs a safe preview/highlight projection that does not write hidden model state.

## 3. In scope
Add proposal-review highlight state keyed to semantic IDs/document references, reveal/focus selected affected item, distinguish existing/modified/created/deleted-preview states where canonical proposal data can represent them, Plan and 3D highlighting, document/sheet affected-state indication, clear preview on reject/close/stale proposal, and handling for hidden/off-level targets with explicit navigation action.

## 4. Out of scope
No canonical mutation, no renderer-only semantic changes, no speculative geometry reconstruction beyond the reviewed proposal/dry-run contract.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
Coordinate Plan/3D selection/highlight and #389 derived-state owner. Keep proposal-review highlight separate from ordinary selection while allowing controlled reveal/select actions.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
Preview/highlight is disposable view state. Any geometry preview must come from canonical dry-run/operation projection APIs, not mutate scene/model stores directly.

## 7. UI/UX states
Existing affected object, proposed create, proposed delete, modified object, hidden/off-level, missing/deleted/stale target, multi-object group, affected sheet/view and cleared review.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
No preview/highlight state persists as project content. Closing/reloading cannot make a proposal appear applied.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
Only permitted project objects may be revealed; no cross-project target leakage from stale Agent context.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
Affected-object list/reveal actions provide non-visual equivalent; highlight state is not colour-only; current reviewed object/status is announced in the Review Centre.

## 11. Performance impact
Large affected sets must use batched/selective highlight and avoid whole-scene material rewrites or expensive per-frame proposal recomputation.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
Proposal fixtures with create/update/delete/hidden/off-level/stale targets, Plan/3D/document reveal parity, clear-preview regression, cross-project isolation and large affected-set performance.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- preview/highlight never mutates canonical project data;
- affected IDs map consistently across Review Centre, Plan, 3D and sheet/browser where supported;
- hidden/off-level items can be revealed without losing review context;
- stale/missing targets are explicit;
- preview clears deterministically on reject/close/invalidation.

## 14. Agent progress updates
Post highlight state owner, projection API used, supported preview classes, performance measurements and browser evidence.

## 15. ZEUS CTO reconciliation notes
#369 verifies proposal preview cannot leak into canonical/renderer authority and remains compatible with normal selection/invalidation.

The UI/UX programme proves the actual first promised ARQ experience as one workflow, not as dozens of individually green components.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
#406 owns the canonical protected Core 1.0 release-gate harness. This issue is the UI/UX acceptance layer that consumes that harness plus UI-specific evidence and refuses UX-6 completion while cross-lane interaction defects remain.

At exact integration head run/extend #406 evidence to exercise through real product surfaces: create/open; active level; author/modify walls; door/window; room; dimension; note; browser/inspector; coordinated 3D; one sheet; scale; PDF export; native Publish; close/reopen; one recovery/failure path. Do not build parallel feature implementations or a second E2E harness. Fix bounded integration defects or open precise child bugs under the owning issue.

No new operations. Verify every user mutation travels existing canonical operation/persistence paths and that cross-view/document outputs converge.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
Use committed/safe fixtures; no private project data in test artifacts.

## 11. Performance impact
Consume #402 workflow budgets and fail/report material regressions rather than calling a slow workflow complete.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
#406 production-bundle harness, relevant UI/browser checks, #400 accessibility evidence, #402 performance, #358-#360 platform envelope and human evidence #211/#408 where required.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- protected workflow completes through real UI on exact integration head;
- no false save/publish/export success occurs;

title: [UX-6.4] Integrate PDF preflight, progress, success and recoverable failure UX
body:

```yaml

risk: high

evidence: [pdf-export-browser, preflight-tests, failure-injection, accessibility-tests]
```

## 1. User outcome
Before exporting, the user can see whether the live sheet is ready; during export, ARQ stays responsive; afterward, success means a real PDF was produced and failure explains what to fix or retry.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
#395 owns canonical scaled vector PDF generation and verification preflight. This issue owns the user-facing preflight and result lifecycle around that real exporter.

## 3. In scope
Render #395 preflight results in the sheet surface, group blocking errors versus warnings, focus/reveal affected viewport/content when possible, expose Export PDF command through canonical commands, show real generation stages/progress where available, support cancel only if exporter contract permits it, distinguish generation versus browser delivery failure, enable safe retry, and show final filename/report without claiming vector/scale success unless #395 verification passed.

## 4. Out of scope
No PDF generation implementation, no print-driver UI, no native project Publish, no silent flattening policy.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
Consume #395 APIs; do not reproduce preflight rules in the UI. Coordinate file-delivery utility ownership and sheet surface owner.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
Export is read-only over project/document state. UI may navigate to problems but does not mutate the model unless the user explicitly performs a separate fix operation.

## 7. UI/UX states
Ready, warnings, blocked by broken reference/invalid scale/missing font/resource/unsupported visible content, generating, generated, delivery failed, cancelled, complete and retry.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
Export state is not project durability state. Failure leaves project unchanged and working-copy status untouched.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
No raw local paths/internal exception dumps. Filenames/content remain local unless the user explicitly shares them through a future feature.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
Preflight list is navigable, problems announced and linked, Export/cancel/retry keyboard accessible, completion/failure status announced without focus theft.

## 11. Performance impact
PDF writer remains deferred/lazy and off the initial bundle as current architecture intends. Preflight should be incremental/worker-backed where needed and must not freeze the editor.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
Real sheet→export browser flow, blocking preflight fixtures, warning-only export, missing font/resource, generation failure, delivery failure, retry, scale verification hand-off and accessibility/focus tests.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- Export command is reachable only through the canonical #395 path;
- blocking preflight prevents misleading success;
- success is shown only after #395 verification;
- generation and delivery failure are distinguishable/recoverable;
- project state is unchanged by export lifecycle.

## 14. Agent progress updates
Post #395 contract consumed, preflight classes surfaced, lazy-load/bundle evidence and all injected failure outcomes.

## 15. ZEUS CTO reconciliation notes

title: [P0/P1] Calibrate and enforce the canonical geometry tolerance ladder
body:
Parent programme: #367
P0/P1 architecture dependency
Depends on: #88 canonical unit/numeric representation
Related product issues: #378, #382, #385, #389, #411, #413

## User outcome
Geometric operations behave predictably across small details, ordinary buildings, large coordinates, imported files and repeated edits. ARQ must not depend on scattered magic epsilons or provisional tolerance magnitudes that happen to pass today's fixtures.

## Current evidence / known gap
ARQ already has a named tolerance policy and geometry functions that take explicit tolerances, but current repository notes state that the actual magnitudes remain provisional pending the canonical numeric/unit decision and domain calibration. Core authoring, dimensions, room boundaries, import reconciliation and future connectors depend on settling this deliberately.

## In scope
After #88 is resolved:
- inventory every named tolerance and every remaining local epsilon/magic threshold across geometry, snapping, topology, BIM operations, imports/exports and rendering-to-model hit tests;
- define one canonical tolerance ladder with purpose-specific fields rather than one global epsilon;
- distinguish at minimum coordinate coincidence, zero-length/degeneracy, intersection/topology, angle, area, snap/display and import/reconciliation tolerances where the architecture requires separate semantics;
- define how tolerances scale or do not scale with canonical units, world extents and view-space interactions;
- measure behaviour on representative architectural extents and adversarial fixtures, including very small details, large site coordinates, near-parallel segments, nearly coincident endpoints, repeated transforms and import round trips;
- document which tolerances are model-semantic and which are UI/view-space only;
- update all Core geometry/operation consumers to use the accepted named policy;
- add a check for forbidden stray model-space epsilons outside explicitly approved modules;
- define compatibility/migration consequences if tolerance changes affect derived topology or validation in existing projects.

## Out of scope
Do not choose the canonical numeric representation here. Do not hide algorithm instability by simply increasing tolerances until tests pass. Do not make screen-pixel snap tolerance a canonical geometric truth.

## Safety rules
- invalid/ambiguous geometry must fail explicitly rather than being coerced into coincidence;
- tolerance changes must not silently rewrite persisted canonical coordinates;
- imported geometry reconciliation must report any approximation that crosses material fidelity boundaries;
- topology-changing tolerance changes require explicit compatibility review.

## Evidence
Benchmark/fixture matrix across representative scales; property/adversarial tests; import/export round trips; wall join/room boundary/dimension reference regression suite; repeated-edit drift tests; exact-head performance measurement.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] #88 is resolved first or this issue remains blocked.
- [ ] One documented named tolerance ladder is accepted and used by Core model operations.
- [ ] No unapproved model-space magic epsilons remain in the scoped packages.
- [ ] Screen/view tolerances are clearly separated from semantic geometry tolerances.
- [ ] Wall joins, room boundaries, stable references and supported import reconciliation pass calibrated adversarial fixtures.
- [ ] Existing project compatibility effects are measured and documented.
- [ ] Changing a tolerance requires targeted evidence and cannot silently weaken validation globally.

## ZEUS CTO reconciliation
#369 must review this together with #88, wall/room/dimension lanes and import adapters because a tolerance change can produce cross-cutting semantic regressions even when each package's unit tests remain green.

body:
Parent programme: #367
Entry: web/Core interaction contracts stable; physical-device evidence available. Related current issue: #359.

## Product outcome
A native iPad experience adds capabilities the web surface cannot reliably provide, rather than merely wrapping the website.

## Capability groups
- native document/Files integration and robust local/offline project handling;
- Pencil hover, double tap, squeeze and haptic feedback only on documented supported hardware/APIs;
- keyboard/trackpad parity for appropriate commands;
- native share/export/open-in flows;
- RoomPlan/LiDAR capture prototype with explicit measurement/coordinate/calibration limitations;

## Principles

title: [EPIC P6] Firm Intelligence: reusable standards, libraries, rules and precedent memory
body:
Parent programme: #367
Entry: stable native model, Agent/Skills contracts and permissions.

## Product outcome
A practice can encode and reuse its own trusted architectural standards without turning informal precedent into hidden AI behaviour.

## Capability groups
- **Firm library:** approved wall/opening/component/types, annotation/document standards and reusable project resources with versioning/provenance.
- **Firm rules:** explicit machine-readable constraints/checks with severity, scope, jurisdiction/project applicability and human override policy.
- **Precedent search:** search the firm's authorised prior projects/resources by semantic attributes and bounded embeddings/metadata, preserving access controls and project provenance.
- **Firm Skills:** versioned P3 Skills owned/published by the practice with review/approval lifecycle.

## Principles
Firm knowledge is separate from model-provider memory. A precedent does not automatically become a design rule. Rules/checks are explainable and source-linked. Access control is enforced at retrieval as well as UI. Updating a library/rule version does not rewrite old project provenance.

## Exit gate
- [ ] Versioned firm library can be applied to new/current projects through explicit operations.
- [ ] Rules produce explainable pass/warn/fail results with source/version.
- [ ] Precedent search respects project permissions and identifies source project/revision.
- [ ] Firm Skills have publish/revoke/version lifecycle.
- [ ] Offline/native projects remain usable when firm services are unavailable; unavailable firm features degrade explicitly.
- [ ] Security/privacy/retention policy is approved for firm data.

## Decomposition rule

## User outcome
After reviewing a valid current proposal, an authorised architect can approve it and ARQ applies exactly the reviewed operation group through the same canonical model, validation, persistence and undo system as manual editing.

## In scope
- approval action with current permission/grant checks;
- revalidate project/revision/preconditions immediately before commit;
- apply the exact reviewed typed operation group, not regenerate a new one at approval time;
- atomic/grouped commit semantics where required;
- one grouped undo/redo entry with meaningful label;
- native persistence acknowledgement and honest save state;
- provenance linking request -> proposal -> approval -> operations -> resulting revision;
- Review Centre result state and links to affected objects;

title: [P1] Handle browser storage quota, low-space and large-project pressure without data-loss ambiguity
body:
Parent: #373
Phase: P1
Related: #397

## User outcome
When local browser storage is constrained, ARQ warns early, explains the difference between working-copy risk and published-file safety, and fails writes predictably without pretending work is durable.

## In scope
- measure available storage where the platform permits it, without treating estimates as guarantees;
- define thresholds for warning/critical states using measured project/resource size;
- distinguish canonical working-copy bytes, recoverable journal/metadata and disposable derived caches;
- reclaim derived/cache data before risking canonical data where policy allows;
- explicit write refusal/failure state when quota prevents acknowledgement;
- recovery/export/publish recommendations that are actually available in the current product;
- large underlay/resource pressure and cancellation;
- browser-specific limitations recorded in the support matrix.

## UX
Persistent but non-blocking warning before critical pressure; blocking error only when a required write cannot be acknowledged. Never show `saved` after quota failure. Provide a clear next action and current risk state.

## Safety
Never delete canonical project data automatically to satisfy quota. Do not promise exact free-space values when browser APIs only provide estimates.

## Evidence
Injected quota/error tests, large project/resource fixtures, cache eviction tests, browser capability checks, restart/recovery after failed writes.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Quota/write failures produce honest unsaved state.
- [ ] Disposable caches can be reclaimed without changing semantic project state.
- [ ] Canonical data is never auto-deleted for space.
- [ ] Warnings/actions match platform capabilities.
- [ ] Failure/recovery behaviour integrates with #397 and publication semantics.

title: [ZEUS PROGRAMME] Enforce the universal issue contract and machine-readable dependency metadata
body:
Parent programme: #367

## Objective

Make every ARQ implementation lane self-contained enough that an agent can safely pick one issue, understand the user outcome, identify dependencies/conflicts, implement it, prove it, update the issue, and hand it back without relying on hidden chat context.

This issue does **not** replace #317/#319. It builds the programme-level issue contract on top of their ownership protocol once available.

## Required issue metadata

Define a stable machine-readable block for programme issues containing at least:

- programme phase;
- parent epic;
- lifecycle state (`blocked`, `ready`, `claimed`, `in_progress`, `review`, `merged`, `verified`, `released`, `human_evidence`, `superseded`);
- dependencies by issue number;
- blocking issues;
- expected ownership surfaces/files/globs if known;
- risk tier;
- required evidence layers;
- user journey / capability IDs;
- release gate impact;
- whether human/external evidence is required;
- whether the issue may be safely worked in parallel;
- next reconciliation checkpoint.

Do not create a second product/evidence authority. This metadata coordinates work and traceability only.

## Agent issue template

Every executable issue must contain these sections:

1. User outcome
2. Current evidence / known gap
3. In scope
4. Out of scope
5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
6. Canonical model / operations impact
7. UI/UX states
8. Persistence / recovery impact
9. Security / privacy impact
10. Accessibility / input impact
11. Performance impact
12. Tests and exact-head evidence
13. Acceptance criteria
14. Agent progress updates
15. ZEUS CTO reconciliation notes

## Progress-update protocol

While an issue is active, its agent must update the issue at meaningful checkpoints with:

- branch and head SHA;
- files/interfaces actually touched;
- assumptions changed after reading code;
- evidence run and result;
- blockers discovered;
- follow-up issue required, if any;
- whether the original scope remains valid.

The issue must not be marked complete merely because a PR was opened.

## Dependency rules

- A blocked issue must not be auto-selected by ZEUS.
- An issue whose dependency has changed materially must be re-preflighted before implementation continues.
- Different issue numbers do not imply safe parallelism. Shared semantic contracts, persistence paths and cross-cutting UI surfaces must be serialised when needed.
- Research-only issues reserve no runtime files unless they become implementation lanes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One canonical programme issue metadata schema exists and is documented.
- [ ] A validator can parse programme issues and reject malformed executable issues.
- [ ] ZEUS issue selection can distinguish ready work from blocked/future work.
- [ ] Dependencies and conflicts are surfaced before mutation begins.
- [ ] The schema composes with #317/#319 instead of duplicating their claim state.
- [ ] The master issue #367 and all newly created programme issues can be represented without losing required information.
- [ ] Tests cover malformed metadata, dependency cycles, stale state, duplicate ownership metadata and blocked-issue selection.
- [ ] Documentation states clearly that product truth still comes from code/ADRs/evidence, not issue metadata.

## Handoff

Once this lands, the ZEUS CTO reconciler should use this contract to refresh programme state and to create later-phase atomic issues only when their phase gate is ready.

Parent: #219 (ARQ-189 browser/device validation matrix)

## Problem

Firefox WebGPU availability is not one uniform "desktop" capability. Current primary evidence differs by OS: stable Windows support exists, stable Apple Silicon macOS support exists in newer Firefox, while Linux and Intel macOS remain non-default/experimental. For each desktop OS in ARQ's intended market, choose one of:
- required with WebGPU
- required with WebGL fallback
- supported with limitations
- deferred / not supported

- Windows
- macOS Apple Silicon
- macOS Intel if still in product scope
- Linux if in product scope

- implementing browser-specific fixes
- adding Firefox Android support
- changing unrelated browser policy

title: ARQFS-003: Add lossless semantic wall operations for reference-format projects
body:
## Problem

Reference-format `.arq` projects cannot safely use the workspace's current `WorkspaceOperation` wall edits.

`WorkspaceOperation` carries only drawn wall centreline geometry and ids. A canonical reference wall also requires semantic identity such as `levelId` and `typeId`, and existing walls can own or affect openings, doors, windows, rooms and other dependent model content. The current native save encoder writes only the flat `{ projectName, walls }` shape.

Therefore treating a rich reference project like the flat editable model would either invent missing semantics or silently discard canonical project content.

## Goal

Create a lossless semantic mutation path for walls in reference-format projects so the editor can make real native edits without flattening the model or guessing project semantics.

## Scope

- Define semantic wall create/update/delete operations against the canonical reference model.
- Carry required level and wall-type identity explicitly. Never infer these from unrelated UI labels.
- Define dependency policy for hosted openings, doors/windows, rooms and other affected content on wall delete or geometry change.
- Preserve untouched levels, wall types, rooms, openings, doors, windows, placed content, services, pathways, views and project metadata byte-semantically where possible and semantically always.
- Add a reference-model encoder/serializer that round-trips the typed canonical model rather than projecting it to the flat wall format.
- Integrate operations with undo/redo and `NativeProjectSession` without duplicating its write queue.
- Reopen published output in an independent worker and prove semantic equivalence for untouched content plus the intended edit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Adding a wall requires explicit valid `levelId` and `typeId` and survives publish/reopen.
2. Moving/updating a wall preserves its semantic identity and all unrelated canonical content.
3. Deleting a wall follows an explicit tested dependency policy for hosted/dependent elements. No orphan references are written.
4. A rich project containing multiple levels, wall types, rooms, openings, doors, windows, placed content and views retains all untouched content after edit/publish/reopen.
5. Invalid or incomplete semantic edits are refused rather than guessed.
6. The workspace can switch #355's reference-project persistence route from refusal to this semantic mutation path once these guarantees are proven.

## Relationship

Follow-up to #355. #355 must remain non-destructive and may persist only the flat native model until this semantic path exists.

title: ARQFS-002: Persist live editor operations through native project sessions
body:
## Problem

The native project write path already exists in `NativeProjectSession.save()`, but the workspace editor does not call it.

Today `App.tsx` applies typed plan operations to in-memory walls and records edit/undo/redo activity only through the IndexedDB demo journal (`PLAN_PROJECT_ID = 'demo-project'`). When a writable native `.arq` project is open, the same edits therefore do not advance the native working copy even though publication/checkpoint infrastructure exists.

There is also a critical format boundary: `NativeProjectSession.save()` currently re-encodes the editable model as the flat `{ projectName, walls }` shape. A reference-format project can contain levels, wall types, rooms, openings, doors, windows, placed content and views. Sending a reference project through the flat encoder would silently discard that richer content. This issue must not introduce that data loss.

## Goal

Connect live editor persistence to native project sessions where the current editor model can be round-tripped without loss, while preserving the current demo/recovery journal when no native project is open and explicitly refusing destructive persistence for richer reference projects until semantic edit operations exist.

## Scope

- Add a single workspace persistence bridge for edit, undo and redo operations.
- For a writable flat native project (`snapshot.document === null`), route the resulting wall state plus the exact typed `WorkspaceOperation` through `NativeProjectSession.save()`.
- Use the existing native session queue. Do not invent a second native save queue.
- Keep the existing IndexedDB plan journal for the no-native-project/demo path.
- For reference-format native projects (`snapshot.document !== null`), do not call the flat native save path. Report the project as not safely editable/persistable by the current wall operation model rather than flattening it.
- Respect read-only native projects. Do not silently fall back to the demo journal and imply the project was persisted.
- Do not report `saved` until the selected persistence authority acknowledges the write.
- Surface native write failure as unsaved/failed state without discarding the editor's visible operation or poisoning later saves.
- Ensure undo/redo use the same persistence path as forward edits.
- Make close/publish semantics account for in-flight editor persistence through the session's existing queue.
- Add focused tests for routing, native edit, undo/redo, failure recovery, reference-format refusal and read-only behaviour.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Opening a writable flat `.arq`, drawing/removing walls, then publishing produces bytes whose reopened model contains those edits.
2. Undo and redo change both the visible plan state and the flat native working copy.
3. A native write failure leaves the UI in an honest unsaved state; a later successful write is still attempted and can recover the session.
4. A read-only native project cannot be presented as saved after an edit attempt.
5. A reference-format project can never be flattened by an editor persistence attempt. The bridge refuses that route until semantic wall operations can preserve levels/types/dependants.
6. With no native project open, the current IndexedDB recovery behaviour remains intact.
7. Tests cover the persistence bridge without duplicating `NativeProjectSession` queue logic.

## Follow-up boundary

Reference-format wall editing needs a semantic operation that carries at least level and wall-type identity and preserves/cascades hosted/dependent content correctly. That work is tracked separately and is a prerequisite to making rich reference projects natively editable.

This issue is intentionally narrower than file-handle write-back to the original user-selected file. It closes the safe editor-to-native-working-copy bridge first.

Updates `playwright` from 1.61.1 to 1.63.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Reporters receive them via testStep.subtitle and testStep.params. For Playwright API

Updates `react-aria-components` from 1.19.0 to 1.21.1
Release notes

Sourced from react-aria-components's releases.

React Aria Components v1.21.0

We're excited to welcome a brand new component to the family! The new NavigationTree component displays a hierarchical set of links, perfect for building sidebars and complex app navigation. It comes fully loaded with keyboard navigation, and support for nested routes.

Menu also gets a big upgrade this release: it now supports async loading and empty states! Load menu items from an API as the user scrolls with the new MenuLoadMoreItem and use renderEmptyState to show an indicator when data is loading or when the menu is empty.

Full Release Notes

React Aria Components v1.20.0

This release includes many new components and features!

  • The new PreviewTrigger component shows a Popover on hover, focus, or long press. Unlike Tooltip, it may include interactive content, useful for hoverable link previews.
  • TokenField (alpha) allows users to enter text with inline tokens. Use it to build AI prompt fields, tag inputs, structured search fields, mention inputs, and multi-select comboboxes.
  • MenuTrigger now supports trigger="contextMenu", enabling accessible context menus via mouse, keyboard, and touch input.
  • A simpler API to implement keyboard shortcuts to useKeyboard.
  • Support for interactive components like textfields inside Table rows.

Finally, the React Aria and React Stately hook documentation has been completely rewritten! The new docs use the same styles as our React Aria Components examples, and show how to use both components and hooks together.

Full Release Notes

Updates `dexie` from 4.4.4 to 4.4.5
Release notes

Sourced from dexie's releases.

Dexie v4.4.5

This is a maintenance release that fixes an issue with indexes named after inherited Object properties and improves authentication recovery in dexie-cloud-addon.

Related Package Releases

Package Version
dexie 4.4.5
dexie-cloud-addon 4.4.14+
dexie-react-hooks 4.4.0+ (no change)
y-dexie 4.4.0+ (no change)
dexie-export-import 4.4.0+ (no change)

Bug Fixes

dexie@4.4.5

  • fix: don't crash when an index is named constructor — Tables with a primary key or index named constructor could cause db.open() to fail with TypeError: indexList.push is not a function. The internal index lookup now uses an object without a prototype, avoiding collisions with inherited Object.prototype properties such as constructor, toString, and valueOf. (#2325, fixes #1920). Contributed by @​tarann26.

dexie-cloud-addon@4.4.14

  • fix: recover from failed refresh-token renewal — When a locally unexpired refresh token is rejected by the server, login() now falls back to the regular fetchTokens authentication path instead of propagating the refresh error. This allows custom authentication integrations to silently obtain new tokens when possible, or trigger their normal login flow when required. OAuth redirect errors continue to propagate normally. (#2326). Fixed by @​liz709 and @​dfahlander.
Commits
  • 22bdff1 dexie@4.4.5

title: Zeus 5: the reading, the plan loop, the spec compiler, and seven dead scripts wired
body:
Five rounds of work on Zeus. Full handoff: `docs/ZEUS-PRIME-INTEGRATION.md`. Phase 0 reading of the repository: `docs/ZEUS-PRIME-INVENTORY.md`.

State: **green, with four disclosed limits.** Not "perfect".

## Problem

Zeus documented a great deal it could not actually do, and could not tell when a claim was a memory.

1. **Nothing Zeus learned reached a later turn.** `.zeus/eval-log.jsonl` was written by one script, read only by a stats printer, had no lesson field, and was empty.
2. **"Verified" was a memory.** Nothing recorded which gate ran, at which round, against which version of the tree.
3. **"Implemented" was a memory too.** Nothing held the work items, so a six-item request reported finished after four left no artifact saying so.
4. **The always-on core had no drift check.** Nothing proved the kernel stayed a faithful subset of the doctrine it compresses.
5. **7 of 39 Zeus scripts could be run by nothing** — no CLI verb, no package script, no hook, no CI step, no importer. Among them the entire delivery pipeline (`zeus-run-state.mjs`), the role planner, the merge guard and the release watcher.
6. **8 of 10 plainly-UI requests routed to no visual module**, so they got no visual requirements, no UI contract and no accessibility reviewer.
7. **Zeus never said what it thought a request meant**, so a misread surfaced only after the work.

## Solution

**The reading, shown before the work.** Every actionable turn opens with how Zeus read the request, what it deliberately did *not* read it as, every inference it made, and the operator's words quoted back unedited — rendered before any classification field, because that is the line that catches a misread. It restates; it never rewrites the request into different words and acts on those. Deterministic and offline: it runs in the hook on every prompt.

**Plan ledger** (`pnpm zeus:plan`). The work items. An item is done only with a command and a zero exit code; `close` refuses while any item is pending, active or blocked, and names each one. That refusal is the loop.

**Spec compiler** (`zeus spec`). A request turned into something precise enough to implement: the routed modules' own requirement prose, the acceptance criteria, the owning role, the checks. It **never invents intent** — everything it cannot derive is a `TODO`, and `spec --check` refuses the file while one remains. For UI work it emits the twelve dimensions `zeus visual-contract` requires as questions, so a generated skeleton cannot satisfy that lint by shape alone.

**Gate ledger** (`pnpm zeus:gate`). Gate results bound to the workspace fingerprint `zeus-fingerprint.mjs` already computed. A failed gate is never skippable; rounds are bounded by the tier's `repairRounds`; `ship` refuses without the repository gate set and, where risk or radius requires review, **a passing review for every reviewer the changed paths call for** — not merely one. Where the paths resolve to no reviewer, a count applies instead: two independent reviews at high risk and above. Derived beats chosen: two reviews by the wrong two specialists satisfy a count and fail this.

**Continual harness** (`pnpm zeus:harness`, proposed by `/zeus-refine`). Supplemental learned state with mandatory evidence, injected into every turn under a character budget, every mutation one rollback away within a 5-refinement window.

**Drift guards** (`pnpm zeus:drift`). The kernel still names every mode, tier, blast radius level, reversibility, evidence state and configured budget; the hook still *runs* the harness; every slash command is skipped; **every Zeus script is reachable**; the published saving is still true.

**Seven dead scripts wired**, plus the org chart: `.zeus/role-registry.json` defined 14 roles and was read by nothing while the engine carried its own copy of the module-to-role map. The registry now owns it and validation enforces it.

**UI routing fixed.** `ui-visual` went from 13 tokens of design-system language to 45 tokens and 16 phrases: 10/10 hit, 0/10 over-match against controls, pinned by 13 regression cases of which 8 fail against the old vocabulary.

## Non-goals

- prime-agent's runtime, daemon, agent-to-agent messaging and bounded autonomous mode. Autonomy is the repository owner's decision, not an agent's.
- A gate runner that executes commands. The ledgers record a claim about a check, not the check.
- Supabase. It is not in this codebase; only `database/` design artifacts exist.

## Tests

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test` | 4075 tests (baseline 3907; +168, zero failures either side) |
| `pnpm typecheck` | 37 of 37 |
| `pnpm lint` | `eslint .`, no output |
| `pnpm format:check` | clean |
| `pnpm build` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm zeus:test` | green |
| `node scripts/zeus-drift-guard-test.mjs` | 24 cases, each guard broken on purpose |
| `node scripts/zeus-classification-test.mjs` | 29 cases |
| `pnpm engineering:context:verify` / `:workflows` / `:policy` | green |

`vitest.config.ts` collects `scripts/**/*.test.ts`, and `ci.yml` runs the drift-guard regression suite, `zeus:drift` and `zeus:validate` in `lint-and-typecheck`. The guard test runs first, on the same principle as `check:decision-ids:test`: a verifier that cannot fail would report a clean repository either way.

**Every new guard was broken on purpose.** Weakening `HARNESS_INVOCATION` to a filename match fails 2 of 24 drift cases, which is how the invocation match is proven to be doing the work.

**Thirty tests were run against deliberately un-fixed modules and all failed as they should.** Five tautologies were caught this way and fixed — including one in the probe that runs those checks, whose import rewrite matched nothing so every run had used the fixed module, and one where a comment explaining the trap re-created it by naming the probe file.

## Performance effect

The hook spawns one extra `node` process per actionable prompt. The harness block is bounded at 1,200 characters. `.zeus/FAST-KERNEL.md` grew from 4,871 to 7,994 bytes and is 84.3% smaller than the doctrine set it compresses; the published floor was lowered from 85% to 80% when the drift guard refused the claim at 84.3%. The harness store was measured at 2,385 KB after 80 ordinary refinements carrying 24 KB of state; bounding the snapshot window brought the same load to 254 KB.

## Accessibility effect

None directly — no product surface is touched. Indirectly positive: UI requests now reach `arq-ux-accessibility-reviewer` and carry the twelve-dimension visual contract, which 8 of 10 previously did not.

## Project format and migration effect

None. No `.arq` reader, writer, schema version or migration path is touched. New state under `.zeus/`: `harness/state.json` is tracked (learned state is human-committed); `gates/` and `plans/` are gitignored, because a result bound to a fingerprint means nothing in another checkout.

## Dependency and licence effect

No dependency added or changed; `pnpm-lock.yaml` untouched. Ideas from `PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent`, MIT, attributed in each module that carries one.

## Security and privacy effect

- Harness entries are scanned for secret shapes and refused; a labelled git object id stays citable, because the evidence rule asks for a commit and the long-hex rule must not then reject one.
- Entry text reaches the hook's output but is only ever carried as a shell variable and printed; bash does not re-scan a variable expansion, so `$(...)` inside an entry stays literal. That property is load-bearing and commented as such.
- `install-zeus.sh` excludes `.zeus/harness/` and `.zeus/gates/`, so installing Zeus elsewhere cannot carry this repository's learned state across.
- The review gate refuses a reviewer name no dispatchable agent could have run, removing the "record `review:me-the-author`, then ship" path at every risk tier.
- `.claude/hooks/**` and `.claude/settings.json` now route to `security` as well as `architecture`.

## Rollback

`git revert` of the merge restores the previous behaviour completely; nothing is compensable or irreversible. The hook degrades safely on its own: every path exits 0, and a corrupt harness store produces a visible warning with 0 bytes on stderr rather than a blocked turn (reproduced with both a malformed and a truncated store). Learned entries roll back individually, including a rollback of a rollback, within the window; beyond it the store is tracked, so git holds the history.

## What is NOT done

1. **No independent reviewer was dispatched.** This session was forbidden from using the Agent tool. Classifying Zeus's own surface changed this diff to **high risk, `production` blast radius**, and `pnpm zeus:gate ship` refuses it by name: `arq-architecture-reviewer`, `arq-release-reviewer` and `arq-security-ai-reviewer` have not passed. That refusal was left standing and red rather than satisfied with a recorded review that never happened. The merge proceeds on the repository owner's explicit instruction, with `engineering-gate` — which `CLAUDE.md` names as the actual merge authority, Zeus being advisory — green on the head commit. **Dispatching those three reviewers against the merged head remains outstanding work.**
2. **Every gate is self-attested.** Recording `typecheck --outcome pass` does not run `tsc`.
3. **`pnpm zeus:test` still does not run in CI**, because it asserts a p95 compile time under 20 ms that would flake on a shared runner. The drift guards, `zeus:validate` and the 147 Zeus tests do run.
4. **The reviewer match is only as good as the impact map.** An uncovered path yields `matched: false` and falls back to a count: fail-closed, but weaker than a match.

## Open questions

1. **Does the agent operating system deserve its own blast radius level?** `.zeus/`, `scripts/zeus-*` and `.claude/` are classified at `product` radius, which closes the fail-open. But `product` means "user-visible product behaviour across packages", and that is not what these files are. A seventh level would describe them honestly and would renumber a scale `zeus-validate.mjs` requires to be contiguous. That is a vocabulary decision.
2. **How much autonomy should the loop have?** The machinery that makes an autonomous loop safe is built — deterministic next-item, mandatory evidence, a refusal to close early. Unbounded self-continuation is deliberately not built.
3. **Should Arq have a Supabase backend at all?** There is none today.

Updates `playwright` from 1.61.1 to 1.62.1
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.62.1

Bug Fixes

  • #41989 [Regression]: tsconfig "extends" bare specifier isn't resolved via node_modules walk-up like tsc (fatal since 1.62)
  • #41998 [Regression]: directory-form tsconfig project references ("path": "../pkg") fail to resolve (fatal since 1.62)
  • #41985 Accessibility snapshot drops button name when text is nested inside spans with aria-hidden SVG
  • #42000 [Regression]: page.evaluate() arg of a branded primitive type (string & { brand }) no longer type-checks since 1.62
  • #42013 [BUG]Image-type actionable elements are not presented in the snapshot.

v1.62.0

🧱 New component testing model

Component testing moves to a stories and galleries model. A story wraps your component in one specific scenario — hard-coded props, mock data, providers — and a gallery page that you serve renders stories on demand. The new fixtures.mount() fixture navigates to the gallery, mounts a story by id, and returns a Locator scoped to the story's root element:

test('click should expand', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount('components/Expandable/Stateful');
  await component.getByRole('button').click();
  await expect(component.getByTestId('expanded')).toHaveValue('true');
});

Pass a story type as a template argument to type-check its props, and use update(props) / unmount() on the returned locator to re-render or tear down within a test.

🛑 Cancel operations with AbortSignal

Most operations and web-first assertions now accept a signal option that takes an AbortSignal, letting you cancel long-running actions, navigations, waits, and assertions:

const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000);

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ signal: controller.signal });
await expect(page.getByText('Done')).toBeVisible({ signal: controller.signal });

Providing a signal does not disable the default timeout; pass timeout: 0 to disable it.

🖼️ WebP screenshots

expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() and expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot() can now store snapshots in the WebP format — just give the snapshot a .webp name:

// Visual comparisons store the golden snapshot as lossless WebP.
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage.webp');

// Standalone screenshots can trade quality for size with lossy WebP.
await page.screenshot({ path: 'homepage.webp', quality: 50 });

Updates `react-aria-components` from 1.19.0 to 1.20.0
Release notes

Sourced from react-aria-components's releases.

React Aria Components v1.20.0

This release includes many new components and features!

  • The new PreviewTrigger component shows a Popover on hover, focus, or long press. Unlike Tooltip, it may include interactive content, useful for hoverable link previews.
  • TokenField (alpha) allows users to enter text with inline tokens. Use it to build AI prompt fields, tag inputs, structured search fields, mention inputs, and multi-select comboboxes.

This is a maintenance release that fixes an issue with indexes named after inherited Object properties and improves authentication recovery in dexie-cloud-addon.

Package Version
dexie 4.4.5
dexie-cloud-addon 4.4.14

y-dexie 4.4.0 (no change)

Bug Fixes

dexie@4.4.5

  • fix: don't crash when an index is named constructor — Tables with a primary key or index named constructor could cause db.open() to fail with TypeError: indexList.push is not a function. The internal index lookup now uses an object without a prototype, avoiding collisions with inherited Object.prototype properties such as constructor, toString, and valueOf. (#2325, fixes #1920). Contributed by @​tarann26.

dexie-cloud-addon@4.4.14

  • fix: recover from failed refresh-token renewal — When a locally unexpired refresh token is rejected by the server, login() now falls back to the regular fetchTokens authentication path instead of propagating the refresh error. This allows custom authentication integrations to silently obtain new tokens when possible, or trigger their normal login flow when required. OAuth redirect errors continue to propagate normally. (#2326). Fixed by @​liz709 and @​dfahlander.

Updates `playwright` from 1.61.1 to 1.62.1
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.62.1

Bug Fixes

  • #41989 [Regression]: tsconfig "extends" bare specifier isn't resolved via node_modules walk-up like tsc (fatal since 1.62)
  • #41998 [Regression]: directory-form tsconfig project references ("path": "../pkg") fail to resolve (fatal since 1.62)
  • #41985 Accessibility snapshot drops button name when text is nested inside spans with aria-hidden SVG
  • #42000 [Regression]: page.evaluate() arg of a branded primitive type (string & { brand }) no longer type-checks since 1.62
  • #42013 [BUG]Image-type actionable elements are not presented in the snapshot.

v1.62.0

🧱 New component testing model

Component testing moves to a stories and galleries model. A story wraps your component in one specific scenario — hard-coded props, mock data, providers — and a gallery page that you serve renders stories on demand. The new fixtures.mount() fixture navigates to the gallery, mounts a story by id, and returns a Locator scoped to the story's root element:

test('click should expand', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount('components/Expandable/Stateful');
  await component.getByRole('button').click();
  await expect(component.getByTestId('expanded')).toHaveValue('true');
});

Pass a story type as a template argument to type-check its props, and use update(props) / unmount() on the returned locator to re-render or tear down within a test.

🛑 Cancel operations with AbortSignal

Most operations and web-first assertions now accept a signal option that takes an AbortSignal, letting you cancel long-running actions, navigations, waits, and assertions:

const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000);

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ signal: controller.signal });
await expect(page.getByText('Done')).toBeVisible({ signal: controller.signal });

Providing a signal does not disable the default timeout; pass timeout: 0 to disable it.

🖼️ WebP screenshots

expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() and expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot() can now store snapshots in the WebP format — just give the snapshot a .webp name:

// Visual comparisons store the golden snapshot as lossless WebP.
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage.webp');

// Standalone screenshots can trade quality for size with lossy WebP.
await page.screenshot({ path: 'homepage.webp', quality: 50 });

title: build(deps): bump wasm-bindgen from 0.2.126 to 0.2.128 in /rust
body:
Bumps [wasm-bindgen](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen) from 0.2.126 to 0.2.128.
Release notes

Sourced from wasm-bindgen's releases.

0.2.128

Added

  • Added OffscreenCanvas overloads for the WebGL texImage2D, texSubImage2D, texImage3D and texSubImage3D functions, matching the TexImageSource typedef in the WebGL specification. #5312

  • Added --split-debug-info to the CLI. This option extracts the DWARF debug info to a separate *_bg.debug.wasm file. Use --debug-info-url to set the recorded URL for the debug info. #5279

  • Added #[wasm_bindgen(experimental_generic_mono)] for imported functions, which binds a generic import once per monomorphisation instead of erasing its type parameters to JsValue. It can be applied to an individual import or to a whole extern "C" block, which every generic function in the block then inherits. Each instantiation gets its own descriptor, so arguments and return values are marshalled at their concrete types (a u32 crosses as a number, a String as a string) rather than being boxed. Trait bounds, where predicates (including higher-ranked ones), associated-type projections, lifetime parameters, argument-position impl Trait, raw callbacks with owned generic inputs and returns, async, catch, and slice_to_array are all supported; see the guide for the supported surface and the shapes that are rejected. The attribute is experimental and may change as it stabilizes. #5230 #5272 #5314

  • #[wasm_bindgen(experimental_generic_mono)] now supports class-level generic parameters: an imported type that is itself generic (type Holder<T>), used as a method receiver (this: &Holder<T>), or as the return type of a constructor or self-returning static method (fn new<T>(value: T) -> Holder<T>). See Class-level generics in the guide. #5290

  • A generic imported type used as a method receiver or a constructor's return type may now carry concrete generic arguments (this: &Holder<u32>, this: &Holder<u32, T>). The arguments are re-emitted as written, so the generated method hangs off impl Holder<u32> rather than the class's own parameter defaults. #5290

  • Added experimental JSPI (JS Promise Integration) support: using it emits a compiler warning noting the experimental status. Supports #[wasm_bindgen(jspi)] on exports (sync or async), within which a #[wasm_bindgen(suspending)] import call can suspend to the JS event loop until its Promise settles. js_sys::futures::jspi_block_on_promise

title: Three things the repository was wrong about, and the gates that let it be
body:
Three defects found by auditing the repository against its own evidence. Each is a case of a surface disagreeing with what the code does; in every case the drift was possible because nothing was checking, so each fix ships with the check that would have caught it.

| # | Defect | Fix |
| - | ------ | --- |
| 1 | Public site says `.arq` projects cannot be opened. They can. | Claim promoted, conflict resolved, five pages corrected, six rendered tests |
| 2 | `NOTICE` says ARQ has no third-party code. It has 289 packages. | Rewritten, both reviewed exceptions named, bound to the SBOM by a new gate |
| 3 | Every reader downloads a PDF writer on first paint. | Deferred; entry chunk −68% gzipped, with a budget and a browser check |

## Problem

**1. The open.** The site told readers that choosing an `.arq` file ends at a compatibility verdict and that opening it "is not wired yet". Three pages carried the denial, `native-arq-open` was `LIBRARY_ONLY`, and `DRIFT-NATIVE-OPEN-MARKETING` was an active **critical** conflict blocking the public, support and documentation surfaces.

That conflict is worth recording in the direction it actually ran. It was opened because copy promised an open the product could not perform; it is closed because that same copy had become the opposite defect — denying an open the product had shipped. The registry caught the overclaim and then went on blocking a claim that had become true. A gate that only fails in the optimistic direction lets the product get quietly better than its own description, which is a nicer failure than lying and is still a failure. The 2026-08-11 marketing UI/UX pass (#309) reworked these very pages and did not catch it, because it audited presentation rather than truth.

**2. The notices.** `NOTICE` — the attribution file `LICENSE` points at — said *"No third-party code has been incorporated into this repository yet - it currently contains planning documentation only"*, with a component table reading `(none yet)`. The build depends on 289 packages across 12 licence families, and `/legal/open-source` lists every one correctly from the same bill of materials the CI licence gate enforces. The repository was telling the truth to the public and the opposite to anyone reading its own legal file. The two packages it most needed to name were the ones missing: `web-ifc` (MPL-2.0) and `caniuse-lite` (CC-BY-4.0), the reviewed exceptions that carry obligations beyond attribution. `docs/product/DEPENDENCY-AND-LICENCE-POLICY.md` records the reasoning for both — the repository knew; `NOTICE` was the only place that did not.

**3. The bundle.** `App.tsx` imported the sheet exporter statically, so pdf-lib, fontkit and their font and encoding tables sat in the start-up chunk, reachable only by invoking the export command. The entry chunk was 1,761.63 kB raw / 743.02 kB gzipped. This is the second time it has been fixed: `4c31107` deferred the 3D surface and reached 614 kB / 193 kB, and it had since grown past the figure that prompted that work. The split was made once and nothing watched it.

## Solution

Each fix is paired with the gate that makes it stick, because in all three cases an unenforced correction is what drifted.

- **Open**: claim → `CURRENT` (bounded to opening), conflict resolved with evidence, three bindings re-moded, two added for pages that now make a current-state claim. Copy corrected on home, product, architects and iPad, plus a dated changelog entry — the superseded 24 July entry points forward rather than being rewritten, since editing it would destroy the record of what was true when.
- **`DECISION-PERSISTENCE-TIERS`**: `unresolved-decision` → `evidence-insufficient`. Still blocking, but ADR-0028/0030 settled the architecture; what is missing is a tested write flow. The two statuses ask for different work — one asks an owner for a decision already made, the other asks an engineer for a checkpoint path that does not exist.
- **`NOTICE`**: states what is incorporated, names both exceptions with the obligation ARQ accepts, lists the licence families. It deliberately does not restate all 289 packages — a hand-maintained copy of generated data is exactly what went stale, and `NOTICE` already carried the instruction not to hand-edit it.
- **Bundle**: the exporter moves behind a dynamic import inside the export handler. 1,762 kB → 754 kB raw, 743 kB → 235 kB gzipped.

## Non-goals

- No save or checkpoint path. Nothing writes back to the chosen `.arq` file, and no surface says otherwise; `portable-arq-publication` stays `LIBRARY_ONLY`.
- No claim about Safari on iPadOS. The open is measured in Chromium on a desktop runner, and the iPad page refuses to generalise from it.
- No licence-grant or repository-visibility decision. `LICENSE-DECISION-REQUIRED.md` records a verified conflict between the recorded decision and the observed repository state; that is an owner decision with legal advice attached and this branch deliberately does not infer one.
- No full STATUS.md reconciliation. Everything outside the claims section still dates from `0336cfa`, ~120 commits back, and now says so rather than presenting stale counts as current.

## Visual evidence

`benchmarks/results/native-open-capability.png` and `native-open-plan.png` re-recorded from this tree. The rendered home page was inspected directly at 1440px and 390px after the copy change.

## Tests

Every guard here was checked by mutation — re-introducing the defect and confirming the guard fails — because a drift gate that silently stops matching recreates the exact failure it was written for, with a green tick over it.

- **Six rendered claim-binding tests**: each page bound to the open claim states the open, and states in the same place that the chosen file is not written to. Re-introducing the old denial and a fabricated save claim each failed the suite. One of those mutations then caught a later copy edit of my own that weakened the limit phrasing.
- **`check:notice-attribution`** (+ 15-case self-test): fails if `NOTICE` denies third-party code while the SBOM reports packages, if a licence family is unlisted, or if a non-blanket-allowed package is unnamed. Run against the original `NOTICE` it produces 14 findings. Includes the OR/AND asymmetry in licence expressions, where being wrong is silent both ways.
- **`check:web-bundle-budget`** (+ self-test): gzipped budget *and* marker-based absence of deferred libraries. Both are needed — a budget alone can be met while a split reverses. Reverting the dynamic import fires both.
- **`benchmark:sheet-export`**: drives the real command palette against the built bundle; asserts the chunk is absent during load and drawing, that the command fetches it, and that the download is a PDF with a page object, painted path operators and its sheet number in metadata.

Writing that last check took four wrong assertions worth recording, each of them me asserting my expectations rather than the code's behaviour: a >1024-byte floor failed a correct 923-byte sheet (the unit test sets 500); a raw `/Type /Page` search missed it because pdf-lib writes object streams; an assertion that the page draws text was wrong twice over, since text is drawn only for text primitives and `SHEET_EXPORT_LIMITATIONS` already says the sheet has no title block; and the sheet number is UTF-16BE inside a hex string, invisible to a latin1 search. The check now inflates the streams and decodes the hex.

Full local run, uncached: 3,907 tests across 352 files, typecheck across 37 packages plus `contracts/`, ESLint, `format:check`, the complete Language System ladder, Engineering OS policy/fixtures/bindings/workflows/context, `zeus-guard-test`, `zeus-security-lint`, the secret, decision-id, registry, boundary and toolchain checks, `benchmark:native-open`, `benchmark:sheet-export`, and `benchmark:marketing-viewport` at 144/144.

## Performance effect

The start-up payload drops from 743.02 kB to 235.27 kB gzipped (−68%); raw entry chunk 1,761.63 kB → 753.97 kB (−57%). The PDF stack is fetched when the export command runs. A 300 kB gzipped budget now guards it, and the marketing site's own budget still passes at 408 kB total dist.

## Accessibility effect

No regression: the marketing viewport check passes keyboard, focus, reduced-motion and WCAG AA contrast across 144 combinations (body text 18.82:1 light / 17.52:1 dark). The new capability check addresses the palette by accessible name (`dialog` "Command palette", `combobox` "Search commands", `option`), so it also fails if the palette loses the combobox/listbox semantics it is built on.

A plain-language gain too: the pages no longer ask a reader to reconcile a site saying the product cannot open their file with a product that opens it.

## Project format and migration effect

None. No format, schema or migration code is touched. The open path itself is unchanged — this describes it accurately. The capability run confirms the reference fixture's SHA-256 is identical before and after, three opens leave one Worker, and closing leaves none.

## Dependency and licence effect

No dependency added, removed or upgraded. The licence *documentation* changes: `NOTICE` now attributes the 12 licence families in the build and names both reviewed exceptions with the obligations ARQ accepts, and a new gate keeps it bound to the bill of materials. A new licence family entering the build now fails a check instead of arriving quietly, which is the review event it should be.

## Security and privacy effect

None adverse. Both capability runs record no off-origin requests and no console errors; the secret scan passes over 2,647 tracked files; `zeus-security-lint` is clean.

Two positives worth naming: a false statement is removed from the page whose subject is where a user's drawings are kept, and the file a downstream consumer would read for third-party obligations now names the MPL-2.0 dependency it previously omitted.

## Rollback

Merged as a squash, `221c33b`, following this branch's `(#NNN)` convention. Rollback is therefore a single `git revert 221c33b`, not the three independent reverts this section described before the merge — corrected rather than left standing, because a rollback plan naming commits that no longer exist is worse than none.

Reverting is atomic by construction rather than by care. Claim state, conflict status and binding modes moved together and revert together, because the language verifiers reject any partial combination: a `current` binding on a non-`CURRENT` claim, or a `CURRENT` claim under an active conflict, each fail the gate. The bundle change reverts to a working, larger bundle, at which point `check:web-bundle-budget` fails — that is the intended signal, not a surprise. No data, schema or deployment state is involved.

To revert only part of it, the four pre-squash commits survive on the `claude/code-review-implementation-bnmp78` branch ref: `29faa2a` (claims and copy), `c7291a8` (`NOTICE`), `891a2c1` (bundle), `8b96d8e` (generated context refresh).

## Known outstanding

Two repository settings, both owner actions rather than code changes, and both the same shape as the defects fixed here — a gate correctly refusing to claim success on evidence it could not obtain.

**GitHub Pages is not enabled**, so the corrected copy is merged but not published. Discovered when this merge triggered the deploy: the `build` job passed, including the rendered-copy audit and the commit-bound deployment proof, and then `actions/deploy-pages` returned `404 … Ensure GitHub Pages has been enabled`. The same job failed identically on `d1e17a1` (#309) and `05424ac` (#308), so it predates this change by at least two PRs. `verify-live-language` was skipped in consequence, meaning no live site was checked either. Fix: Settings → Pages, then re-run the deploy workflow.

**`VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET` is not configured**, so `verify-routes` fails on this branch and on its base: the preview origin serves a sign-in page and the check refuses to report on routes it never saw. Detail in [this comment](https://github.com/ruddvz/Arq/pull/310#issuecomment-5250562067).
