title: Arq Language System 4.1 (Z Voice): one governed vocabulary, gated claims, deployed-site proof
body:
## Problem

The public site said things the repository could not support, and nothing checked it.

- The deployed site carried 132 rendered U+2014 em dashes across its 18 routes.
- `/` said an `.arq` file "opens in your browser" while `FileOpenPanel` stops at a compatibility verdict and the OPFS worker is never constructed.
- `/` also collapsed the IndexedDB demo journal into "saving is a local write" on a `.arq` file, which are two different persistence tiers.
- `/interoperability` said "every import in Arq produces an import report" while no import path is reachable from the product.
- `/security` said the build "sends nothing anywhere" with no network-observation evidence.
- `/students` said "a modest laptop is enough" with no published hardware profile.
- `/pricing` and `/status` gave lifetime guarantees ("can never lock you out", "our outage can never be your outage") that no commercial or architectural decision backs.
- `/product` published "175 tests" and an affirmative "full IFC authoring" with no negation in the sentence.
- `STATUS.md` asserted both a wired 3D tab and a 3D stack with zero consumers, so any surface could quote whichever half suited it.
- CI checked TypeScript source only. A source-only pass could coexist with a stale or non-compliant deployed site.

## Solution

Install Arq Language System 4.1, named Z Voice, as a versioned, source-owned, machine-checkable layer, then bring the copy in line with it.

**Truth before wording.** Nine conflicts are active in `docs/product/voice/conflict-registry.json` and block their claims from public, support, documentation and product-AI surfaces. Two are deliberately left unresolved because they cannot be settled from inside this change:

- `CONFLICT-3D-CURRENT-STATUS`. `ModelCanvas.tsx` exists and `App.tsx` renders it for a `3d` tab, but no test covers that surface and no headless-browser check exercises it, so there is no reachability evidence of the kind the wall-drawing, OPFS and file-open claims have. `STATUS.md` now records the dispute instead of asserting either side, and no public page states 3D as available or as absent.
- `DECISION-PERSISTENCE-TIERS`. ADR-0019/0024 commit to SQLite-WASM over OPFS while `packages/local-storage` ships a tested Dexie/IndexedDB implementation. That needs an ADR from the architecture owner. Until it exists, no surface may describe a journal write as a portable `.arq` write.

**Public copy.** Every em dash removed by rewriting the sentence, not substituting the character: full stops, colons, parentheses, restructuring. `docs/product/voice/PUBLIC-COPY-REMEDIATION-4.1.md` drove the rest, page by page. `/interoperability` now uses Arq's eight fidelity results (Preserved, Converted, Approximated, Flattened, Omitted, Unsupported, Retained as opaque data, Failed). Each changelog entry cites the repository paths or checks behind it. The self-attesting register ("honest", "genuinely", "will not pretend") is gone: the pages state the source, the behaviour or the limit instead.

**Product UI.** `describeSaveState` names the persistence tier ("Saved locally", "Saving locally...", "Recovered locally") because a bare "Saved" read as a portable `.arq` write. `formatCoordinates` returns "Off canvas" rather than a lone dash, matching its sibling "No snap" / "No selection". `state-language-map.json` gains the `web-plan-journal-status` machine so every visible save state reaches a canonical message.

**Machinery.** 21 checks under `scripts/`, 18 pnpm scripts, canonical data under `docs/product/voice/`. The generated context is hashed from the 29 source sets in `context-contract.json`.

**CI and deployment.** A `language-system` job runs the checks in the documented order and never regenerates the committed context: a stale context must fail and be refreshed by the change that moved its sources. The Pages workflow verifies route coverage before the build, audits the rendered output, writes a commit-bound proof with a sha256 per route into the artifact, exposes `page_url`, and runs a post-deployment job that reads the proof and every route back off the published URL and requires the exact SHA (8 attempts, 5s apart).

## Z Voice verification (second commit)

The voice system is also recorded under its name Z Voice in `docs/product/voice/README.md` and `docs/product/VOICE-SYSTEM.md`. An exhaustive check of the integration archive against the repo: all 151 files accounted for (43 byte-identical, 60 differing only by Prettier formatting, 31 deliberate adaptations reviewed diff by diff, 0 missing); the CI fragment's commands match the `language-system` job exactly; every gate in the Pages fragment is present, plus direct verifier invocations the fragment did not require; 20 of 20 fragment pnpm scripts, 6 of 6 claim-gate tests, the guardian hook and the package manifest are all consumed or recorded; every repo path cited by the registries exists. Eleven scripts kept package-layout bare-invocation defaults that failed without flags; their defaults now resolve the repo layout and all 12 verifiers pass when run bare from the repository root, with wired invocations unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Resolving the 3D conflict. That needs a browser capability check for the 3D tab, not a copy edit.
- Deciding the persistence-tier ADR, publishing pricing, or writing legal terms and the privacy notice. Those need their owners.
- Building a runtime support bot or any AI feature. The answerability outcomes (ANSWER, QUALIFY, CONFLICT, UNKNOWN, REFUSE_AUTHORITY) ship as a tested, documented integration boundary with no consumer.
- Reformatting or rewording docs outside the language system's surfaces.

## Visual evidence

Headless-Chromium pass over all 17 public routes plus the 404, at desktop (1440) and 320px, on the built output served under `/Arq`: every route resolves, one `h1` each, no horizontal overflow, no external resource, no failed request, no U+2014 in rendered text.

Rendered em dash count by route, before and after:

| Route | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `/` | 8 | 0 |
| `/product` | 9 | 0 |
| `/architects` | 12 | 0 |
| `/students` | 9 | 0 |
| `/collaboration` | 5 | 0 |
| `/ai` | 11 | 0 |
| `/interoperability` | 7 | 0 |
| `/ipad` | 6 | 0 |
| `/pricing` | 6 | 0 |
| `/security` | 9 | 0 |
| `/docs` | 7 | 0 |
| `/changelog` | 12 | 0 |
| `/status` | 4 | 0 |
| `/contact` | 6 | 0 |
| `/legal/privacy` | 5 | 0 |
| `/legal/terms` | 5 | 0 |
| `/legal/open-source` | 5 | 0 |
| `/404` | 6 | 0 |
| **Total** | **132** | **0** |

Also verified: `pnpm benchmark:workspace-layout` passes at all 8 viewports with the longer save-state labels (result committed under `benchmarks/results/`).

## Tests

Green locally at the current head: `pnpm test` (244 files, 2038 tests), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` (36 packages plus `contracts/`), `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm check:workspace-registries`, `pnpm check:dependency-licences`.

Language ladder, all passing: `arq:language:sources:verify`, `install:verify`, `public:verify`, `routes:verify`, `editorial:verify`, `context:verify`, `data:verify`, `state:verify`, `adapters:verify`, `conflicts:verify`, `claims:verify`, `verify`, `audit:ci`, `bundle:verify`, and `site:build:verify` against `apps/marketing/dist`.

The deployed-site verifier was exercised against a local server holding the built artifact: it passes on the correct commit and fails on a wrong one.

`pages.test.ts` gains the claim-gate suite: public current-state assertions must bind to a non-blocked claim record, each public binding must appear in the inventory, each rendered route must map to exactly one inventory entry, no page may render U+2014, release-ladder text must be labelled as scope, compatibility must not read as an opened project, and the 3D conflict must not be settled in either direction.

**Live GitHub Pages verification has not run on this branch.** The `github-pages` environment restricts deployments to the base branch, so `deploy` is refused here and `verify-live-language` is skipped. Merging this PR puts the change on the base branch, where the environment permits deployment and the live check runs.

## Performance effect

None expected. No runtime code path changed; the site is still static with no JavaScript required. The additions are build-time and CI-time checks.

## Accessibility effect

Small improvement. `formatCoordinates` now returns "Off canvas" instead of a bare em dash, which a screen reader announced as nothing. Save-state labels stay in the same `aria-live` region and remain plain words. The per-page landmark, skip-link, single-`h1` and focus assertions are unchanged and still pass.

## Project format and migration effect

None. No `.arq` schema, migration or recovery code changed. The change makes the language rules around those states stricter: a journal write may no longer be described as a portable-file write, and compatibility preflight may no longer be described as an opened project.

## Dependency and licence effect

None. No dependency added or removed. The licence gate and SBOM run unchanged, and `/legal/open-source` still renders from the generated SBOM.

## Security and privacy effect

Net positive. `/security` and `/legal/privacy` no longer make absolute transport claims the repository cannot evidence; they state the current architecture and name the missing network-observation test. The rendered and deployed verifiers fail the build if any public page loads a third-party script, style, image, font, frame or CSS `url()`, which turns the "no third-party resource" privacy statement into an enforced property rather than an assertion.

## Rollback

Revert the merge. Nothing is generated into the repository outside it, the pnpm scripts and CI jobs are additive, and the previous copy returns with the revert. To keep the language system but stop deploying from the in-flight branch, remove it from the `on.push.branches` list in `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`.

title: Full-repo audit and completion: website, interactive canvas, validation, persistence, 3D view, real quality gates
body:
## Problem

A full-repository audit (8 parallel area audits) found the library layer strong and green but the product thin: the marketing website was 0 of 17 spec'd pages (`apps/marketing` was literally `export {}`), the canvas was a static painting, `@arq/validation` was an `export {}` stub, five data-layer libraries (including local-storage and the whole 3D stack) had zero consumers, the `ifc` format routed to an adapter id that did not exist, planning docs still described the repo as a spec-only ZIP, and several quality gates were fictional (`pnpm lint` ran zero tasks; three CI workflows were `echo` stubs).

## Solution

Ten commits, two rounds.

**Round 1 — foundations:**
1. **Public website** — all 17 PUB sheets from `docs/pages/` plus 404, static, no client JS, designed as an architectural drawing set; honesty enforced by tests (route coverage, landmarks, no external resources, launch-claims checklist as a failing test). Undecided facts (pricing/legal/status) publish the state of the decision, not placeholder fiction.
2. **Interactive canvas** — pan/zoom (wheel, pinch, space-drag), the ARQ-094 wall chain tool over the ARQ-045..052 snap pipeline with live glyphs, hit-test selection, fit; typed operations with real inverses on the undo stack.
3. **Docs truth pass** — new `STATUS.md`, backlog indexes regenerated to all 242 issues via a checked-in generator, ZIP-era root docs rewritten, ~12 READMEs corrected in both directions.
4. **Real quality gates** — eslint over the whole repo (first run caught a real bug), secret scan (1,810 files) in a real Security workflow, explicit Build workflow, honest weekly Benchmark workflow, `contracts/` typechecked. The new licence gate promptly caught eslint's `minimatch` Blue Oak licence — allow-listed through the policy's own process.

**Round 2 — completing the product loop:**
5. **`@arq/validation` implemented** (§4.3): wall-segment, unique-id and room-polygon rules with the product's error structure; consumed at the commit gate with plain-language notices; status-bar model-health counts computed from the real rules. Canvas state language completed per the monochrome rule (distinct line weight/dash per token, tests assert no state is indistinguishable); hover and marquee window/crossing selection with multi-select flowing through the shell.
6. **Real local persistence** — edits journal to IndexedDB via `@arq/local-storage` (ADR-0006 pattern) and recover on reload; save state reports the journal's true condition (`saved`/`saving`/`recovered`/`unsaved-changes`). Verified: draw, reload → recovered; delete, reload → persisted.
7. **3D view** — the workspace's 3D tab renders drawn walls as extruded solids (`geometry-3d` over `wallOutline`, 100 mm/2400 mm) in real WebGL via `@arq/model-renderer`, with orbit/pan/zoom/fit and raycast picking; selection is shared with the plan by construction (`applySharedSelection`).
8. **IFC bridged into the import pipeline** — `IfcIngressAdapter` (the `ifc-ingress` id `formats.ts` always routed to) wraps the real web-ifc reader, registered in the worker's default registry, honestly scoped to viewing/inspection with the policy size limit enforced before the WASM boundary.
9. **Critique passes** — five real defects found by driving the built app and adversarially reviewing my own additions, all fixed: wall tool dead after its first committed chain; double-click leaving a zero-length segment; undo leaving dangling selections (primary and secondary); pinch firing a phantom selection through a stale marquee; a non-brand colour in the 3D selection treatment.

## Non-goals

The `.arq` open-project pipeline (file-open → OPFS worker → workspace), export paths, sync backend/`apps/api`, and co-authoring remain open and are tracked honestly in `STATUS.md`.

## Visual evidence

Headless-Chromium runs against real builds at every step: website (1440/375/320 px, light+dark), wall drawing with snap glyphs, duplicate-wall warning notice with "1 warning" in the status bar, marquee multi-select → "Delete 2 walls", journal recovery across reloads ("Recovered · 2 operation(s) recovered"), and the 3D tab with orbit + click-to-select syncing to tree/inspector/context bar (SwiftShader WebGL).

## Tests

`pnpm test`: 243 files, **2,023 tests, all passing** (193 new this PR). `pnpm typecheck`: 36/36 packages + contracts. `pnpm lint`: real and green. `pnpm format:check`: clean.

## Performance effect

Site is static HTML with self-hosted latin-subset fonts (~140 KB). Canvases paint on state change only (no animation loops); 3D renders on demand and disposes geometry/materials on rebuild. Render benchmarks unchanged, now scheduled weekly in CI.

## Accessibility effect

Site pages: skip link, landmarks, single `h1`, reduced-motion, 320 px/200 % zoom, `prefers-color-scheme`. Workspace: validation notices use `role="status"`; both canvases have `aria-label`s; drawn-wall selection reuses `describeSelectedElementForAccessibility`; selection state is never colour-only (line treatments in 2D, opacity treatment in 3D).

## Project format and migration effect

No `.arq` schema changes. New: an IndexedDB operation journal (ADR-0006 pattern, `arq-local-db`) for the workspace document — append-only, replayed on boot, isolated per project id.

## Dependency and licence effect

Added dev-only at root: `eslint`, `typescript-eslint`. `apps/web` gains workspace deps (`validation`, `local-storage`, `model-renderer`, `geometry-3d`) plus `three@0.185` (already in the tree via model-renderer) and `fake-indexeddb` (dev). `BlueOak-1.0.0` added to the licence allow-list (policy doc + enforcing script together). Licence scan green; SBOM feeds the site's notices page.

## Security and privacy effect

Net positive: real secret scanning (PR + weekly); IFC bytes are size-gated before the WASM boundary with the worker as the documented kill switch; the site loads zero third-party resources and says so on its privacy page. All project data remains local.

## Rollback

Revert the commits in reverse order; each front is independently revertible. The IndexedDB journal database (`arq-local-db`) is regenerable user-local state — deleting it loses only demo-workspace edits. No migrations to unwind.

title: Complete the workspace: touch compositions, panel systems, controls and a critique pass
body:
## Problem

#279 built the workspace spine but left it half-usable, and said so. Its own known-gaps list named the holes: the touch bands were canvas-first but the browser and inspector were closed with **no control to summon them** — a panel you cannot open does not exist. The browser and inspector were single undifferentiated panes despite the registry naming their sections since 3.0 landed. Several tested reducers — tab reorder, duplicate, close-others, panel resize — had no UI at all.

This closes every one of them, audits the result, and closes the gaps that audit created.

## Solution

Six slices, each verified in a real browser before the next.

**1. The touch bands become usable.** New sheet layer in `@arq/workspace`: one open sheet at a time, peek/half/full detents read from the registry's own `sheetDetents`, and a system-back handler that reports whether it *consumed* the gesture — an unconsumed back must reach browser history or an Android user is trapped. Each band gets the presentation its own doc specifies, all from one `SheetState`: landscape tablet → side drawers, portrait tablet and phone → bottom sheets, phone → the full `Select | Tools | View | Review | More` dock.

Two compositions were **replaced rather than adapted**, because they were the wrong shape and not merely too wide:

- The desktop top bar measured **173px at 393px wide**, wrapping to three rows against the registry's 48px. `PhoneProjectBar` is doc 47's composition. **Canvas share went 61% → 76%.**
- The tab strip rendered one tab plus a `+1` overflow on a phone, hiding the user's location behind a menu. Doc 34 wants "a compact current-view control plus a full-height View Switcher"; both now exist.

**2. Browser and inspector section systems** (docs 39, 40). The four registry browser sections and five inspector tabs, as real tablists. Doc 34's rule — "default to the most relevant for context while preserving the user's manual selection" — is two requirements that pull against each other, so both are modelled explicitly. A remembered choice the new context cannot offer is dropped: a Type tab cannot outlive the selection it was the type of.

**3. The controls the registries already described** (docs 36, 37, 51). Tab context menu, panel resize with the ARIA window-splitter pattern, `close-tab`/`fit` wired, palette showing platform-adapted bindings. Escape closes an open sheet *before* cancelling a tool draft — doing both at once would discard work the user only meant to uncover.

**4. Workspace layout capability check** (doc 52) — the eight-viewport sweep, committed and running in CI.

**5. Critique pass** — five defects found by auditing the live DOM (below).

**6. The last five shell gaps**, closed after the critique:

- **Docking preference.** A band closing a panel is a presentation decision, not the user's, and the two were indistinguishable. `dockedPreferenceOpen` restores the panels after a window crosses the tablet band and back, while one the user closed deliberately stays closed.
- **Compact-desktop collapse.** `planTopBarLayout` measures the rendered controls and folds the lowest-priority into an overflow menu in doc 36's stated order, with project identity and active view structurally protected. 900px collapses save state; 760px collapses save, sync and share; the protected pair survives at every width.
- **Sheet drag**, snapping to the nearest registry detent, built on top of the grabber button rather than replacing it.
- **Tree virtualisation** — doc 39's "5,000-element model must not render every row".
- **Tab reordering** — pointer drag and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Arrow.

## Non-goals

- Not building the remaining 27 of 30 surfaces, 43 of 54 tools, 175 of 215 icons or 133 of 147 components.
- Not drawing placeholder glyphs — Package 3.0 is explicit that a generated placeholder is not ARQ artwork.
- Not enabling any capability gate that lacks a backing system.
- Not building split view: `supportsSplit` exists in the registry but there is no split viewport host, so the context menu omits it rather than offering a disabled control for a capability that does not exist.

## Visual evidence

`pnpm benchmark:workspace-layout` — all 8 QA-fixture viewports pass, in CI:

| Viewport | Band | Canvas | Docked | Rails |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1920 × 1080 | desktop | 1010 | 2 | 2 |
| 1536 × 864 | desktop | 626 | 2 | 2 |
| 1366 × 768 | desktop | 754 | 1 | 2 |
| 1024 × 768 | compact-desktop | 412 | 1 | 2 |
| 1194 × 834 | tablet-landscape | 1178 | 0 | 0 |
| 834 × 1194 | tablet-portrait | 818 | 0 | 0 |
| 393 × 852 | phone | 377 | 0 | 0 |
| 412 × 915 | phone | 396 | 0 | 0 |

Zero ARIA structure problems in the rendered DOM. No console errors, no horizontal overflow at any width.

Virtualisation measured against a real 5,000-element fixture: **5,005 rows, 20–29 in the DOM**, `aria-setsize` reporting the true total, scrollbar honest at 180,180px.

## Tests

`pnpm test`: **1849 passing** (1763 before). 109 new behavioural tests across `sheet-state`, `inspector-tabs-state`, `browser-panel-state`, `collapse-priority`, `tree-virtualisation` and `panel-layout-state`. Typecheck clean across 36 packages.

## The critique pass

Asked to review my own work, I audited the real DOM rather than re-reading the source. **Five defects, all fixed:**

1. **ARIA violation.** The `tablist` contained a focusable close button that was not a `tab`, so every closeable tab added a Tab stop — ten views cost twenty presses — and my own doc comment claiming "only the active tab is in the Tab order" was false. Close is now out of the Tab order with Delete as the keyboard path, announced in the tab's accessible name.
2. **`aria-modal` claimed without containment** — the exact bug `ArqModalDialog` exists to prevent, reimplemented by hand. The shell is now `inert` at the full detent, which makes the claim true *and* removes the need for a focus trap.
3. **Tablet drawer announced `role="dialog"` with no keyboard dismiss.**
4. **No skip link** — twenty-plus stops to reach the canvas.
5. **Dead speculative API surface**, two pieces carrying doc comments claiming they were "exposed for the registry-integrity test" — a test that never referenced them. Dead code with a false justification is worse than dead code.

Three more were caught by tooling while building the later slices: `PhoneProjectBar` hardcoding "Unsaved changes · Offline" for a project that was never open; a collapse plan that oscillated forever because a `display: none` slot measures zero and reads as "it fits now"; and an edit that silently failed to apply because prettier had reflowed the target string, leaving the measurement effect a no-op.

## Performance effect

Bundle 228 → 322 kB (+94 kB, gzip 66 → 95 kB) for the touch compositions, both panel systems, the context menu, resize, collapse planning and virtualisation. The large registries stay out of the bundle. CSS 2.78 → 4.56 kB.

Virtualisation is a net win at scale: a 5,000-element level renders ~30 rows instead of 5,000.

## Accessibility effect

The main axis of this PR. One Tab stop per tablist; skip link; `aria-modal` only where `inert` makes it true; menus move focus in and restore it out; every disabled control puts its reason in the accessible name, not only a `title`; 44px touch minimum preserved on coarse pointers.

**Every gesture has a keyboard equivalent** — tab reorder is Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Arrow as well as a drag (and a bare Arrow still navigates, so reorder cannot happen by accident); panel resize is Arrow/Home/End; sheet detents are a button; tab close is Delete, the context menu, Cmd/Ctrl+W and the palette. The virtualiser keeps the focused row mounted, because unmounting it drops focus to `<body>`.

## Project format and migration effect

None. `@arq/workspace` still cannot reach the model or operation log, holds no async work and performs no I/O.

## Dependency and licence effect

None. No new third-party dependencies.

## Security and privacy effect

None. Capability gates remain conservative — the phone dock's Review entry renders disabled with its reason rather than pretending collaboration exists.

## Rollback

Five independent commits, each revertable alone. Everything new is additive: new files in `packages/workspace/src` and `packages/design-system/src/workspace`, plus optional props on `WorkspaceRoot` that default to the previous behaviour, so a host passing none of them renders exactly the old shell.

title: Settle the two flagged platform decisions: defer Tauri (ADR-0027), close the storage-conflict note
body:
## Problem

The 2026-07-24 pack triage (#278) left two platform questions marked "raise with the user before anything moves": a Tauri desktop shell (the pack's ADR-008), and the SQLite-WASM-vs-Dexie storage conflict flagged in `docs/research/incoming/README.md`. The user has now delegated the call. Inspecting the authoritative state showed the two questions were in different conditions than the notes claimed: the storage conflict was already resolved in `docs/product/DECISION-REGISTER.csv` (D-007 superseded, D-015/D-020/D-023) with shipped code (`packages/arqfs`, `workers/arqfs-worker`, OPFS benchmarks) — the README note was stale and kept re-opening a settled question. The Tauri question had the opposite problem: no recorded decision anywhere, so every incoming planning pack re-proposes it and the `@arq/workspace` registries could only point at a "repository decision" that didn't exist.

## Solution

- **`docs/adr/0027-desktop-shell-deferral.md` (new, Accepted):** Arq ships as a browser application; no Tauri package, toolchain, or build target is added now. Records three explicit revisit gates (capability beyond OPFS/File System Access/PWA, measured WebView parity failure for an approved requirement, confirmed distribution requirement) and the adoption conditions if a gate ever passes (pinned versions, least-privilege capabilities, browser-fallback capability port, no `macOSPrivateApi` in default distributables, native renderer stays a separate decision).
- **`docs/product/DECISION-REGISTER.csv`:** new row D-024 registering the deferral with evidence pointers.
- **`docs/research/incoming/README.md`:** rewrote the stale "one real, unresolved architectural conflict" section as "since resolved," documenting the actual resolution (Dexie narrowed to the derived-cache tier per ADR-0022, nothing discarded, cutover awaits its own issue; SQLite `.arq` canonical per D-015/D-020/D-023) so future sessions stop re-raising it as open.
- **Pack triage README:** recommendation 3 updated from "ask the user first" to pointing at ADR-0027/D-024, keeping the pack's `native-desktop-port.ts` as starting material if a gate ever passes.

## Non-goals

- No Tauri code, dependency, or toolchain added — this PR *prevents* that until a gate passes.
- No storage code touched: `@arq/local-storage` and `@arq/arqfs` are both unchanged; the Dexie cutover still awaits its own separately-numbered issue as D-007 specifies.
- No change to any other ADR's status.

## Visual evidence

N/A — documentation and decision-register only.

## Tests

No source code changed. Verified `prettier --check .` clean repo-wide at the lockfile's Prettier 3.9.6, and the register CSV parses with 24 well-formed rows.

## Performance effect

None.

## Accessibility effect

None.

## Project format and migration effect

None — the `.arq` SQLite decisions (D-015/D-020/D-023) are recorded as already made elsewhere; this PR only removes a stale note that contradicted them.

## Dependency and licence effect

None — and ADR-0027 explicitly blocks a new Rust/Tauri toolchain until gated evidence exists.

## Security and privacy effect

Reduces future risk: ADR-0027 pre-commits any eventual shell adoption to least-privilege capabilities and excludes `macOSPrivateApi` from default distributables.

## Rollback

Revert the single commit; it adds one ADR, one CSV row, and edits two research READMEs.

title: Build the open-project workspace from UI/UX Package 3.0/4.0
body:
## Problem

Package 2.5 covered public pages, account pages and individual editor screenshots. It did not cover the thing an architect actually spends the day inside: the persistent workspace that exists after a project opens — modes, view tabs, project browser, inspector, canvas, tool system, status and the transitions between them.

Package 3.0 rebuilt the specification around that, and 4.0 added a visual-refinement layer on top. In this repository the editor was still a flat `App.tsx` composition: a top bar, a rail, a panel and a canvas side by side, with no concept of a project you stay inside while moving between views.

## Solution

Lands the machine-readable half of Packages 3.0/4.0 as an implementation contract, then builds the workspace spine on it.

**New `@arq/workspace` package** — pure TypeScript, no React, no DOM, and deliberately no dependency on `@arq/bim-core` or `@arq/operations`. That absence is load-bearing: doc 33 requires "no layer duplicates canonical model state", and a package that cannot reach the model cannot mirror it.

- The 13 `workspace-*.json` registries, checked in verbatim, with a test that fails the build when the JSON and the TypeScript disagree.
- **View tabs**: open, activate, close, pin, reorder, duplicate, overflow. The registry's headline rule is that closing a tab closes a view *instance*, not the view — so `closeTab` returns new state and nothing else, with no callback or channel through which it could become a deletion.
- **Panel layout**: registry-driven width bounds, and doc 46's per-band docking policy applied *before* doc 36's canvas floor (the touch layouts declare no floor, so deciding floor-first is what previously let an iPad render two docked columns). On the docking bands panels float, never close.
- **Mode, tool and capability state**, each unavailable control carrying the sentence that explains it.

**Workspace shell in `@arq/design-system`**: `WorkspaceRoot`, `ModeRail`, `ProjectTabStrip`, `ProjectOverviewSurface`. Everything else converges the repository's existing `TopBar`, `ToolRail`, `ModelPanel`, `InspectorShell`, `ContextBar` and `StatusBar` rather than duplicating them, per the execution prompt's §0. `ToolRail` gains the registry's eighth (Review) category — appended, so the blueprint's fixed seven keep their indices — and per-tool `disabledReason`.

**Honest status, enforced rather than asserted:**

- `TOOLS_WITH_REPOSITORY_BACKING` names the **11** tools this repository can actually perform, each annotated with its implementing module. All 54 registry tools are shown; the other 43 render disabled saying they are designed but not built. `dimension` has an icon and a rail slot and is deliberately not claimed — a test asserts that.
- `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_CAPABILITIES` enables only `CAP-core-plan`. 3D, document and exchange stay off despite prototypes existing in this monorepo; a prototype is not a capability claim.
- Project Overview renders only cards its data supports, so a build with no model-health engine gets no model-health card rather than a reassuring pair of zeros.
- `pnpm check:workspace-registries` gates registry integrity and prints designed-vs-built coverage, without ever failing on the gap.

**Three defects that verification caught, fixed here:**

1. The app only ever imported `tokens.css`, never `shell-controls.css` — every `.arq-shell-button` in the shell was rendering unstyled. The built CSS goes from 0 to 2.78 kB.
2. The canvas floor used the registry's 48px tool rail while the rendered rail is 200px, leaving it ~150px optimistic — it could stay silent while the canvas was already below its minimum.
3. The tablet bands rendered two docked columns, reducing an 834px iPad to a **zero-width canvas** with horizontal page overflow.

## Commits

Reviewable in order; the third is mechanical and can be skipped.

1. **`Build the open-project workspace from UI/UX Package 3.0/4.0`** — the actual change.
2. **`Update pnpm-lock.yaml for the new @arq/workspace links`** — two new internal workspace links.
3. **`Add .prettierignore and clear the pre-existing formatting drift`** — see Non-goals.

## Non-goals

- Not building the remaining 27 of 30 surfaces, 43 of 54 tools, 175 of 215 icons or 143 of 147 components. Those stay specification-only and are recorded as such.
- Not drawing placeholder glyphs for missing icons — Package 3.0 is explicit that generated placeholders are not ARQ artwork.
- Not enabling any capability gate that lacks a backing system.
- Not authorising Tauri or native mobile packaging (`CAP-native` stays off).
- **Not a redesign of the shell's appearance.** Package 4.0's visual-refinement layer (docs 55–58 and the seven boards) is a target; this delivers the structure those boards describe, not their finish.

## Visual evidence

Headless Chromium against the production build, at the eight viewports `workspace-qa-fixtures.json` lists:

| Viewport | Band | Canvas | Docked panels |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 1920 × 1080 | desktop | 1022 | 2 |
| 1536 × 864 | desktop | 638 | 2 |
| 1366 × 768 | desktop | 760 | 1 (+1 floating) |
| 1024 × 768 | compact-desktop | 418 | 1 (+1 floating) |
| 1194 × 834 | tablet-landscape | 1178 | 0 |
| 834 × 1194 | tablet-portrait | 818 | 0 |
| 393 × 852 | phone | 377 | 0 |
| 412 × 915 | phone | 396 | 0 |

No console errors and no horizontal document overflow at any viewport. The 1920 and 1536 canvases clear their registry floors (900 and 620). Project Overview was confirmed rendering exactly one card — the only one the demo data supports.

## Tests

`pnpm test`: **211 files / 1641 passing**, up from 201 / 1512. 129 new tests, all behavioural rather than snapshot:

- `view-tabs-state` (23) — including that a duplicated view survives its sibling tab closing, and that overflow never hides the active tab nor silently drops a pin.
- `panel-layout-state` (17) — floor behaviour, float-don't-close, width preserved across float and re-dock, and the three touch bands.
- `responsive` (13) — the eight QA viewports classified, pointer-driven rather than device-driven, and the rendered-vs-registry rail width.
- `tool-state` (18), `registry` (12), `mode-state` (11), `keyboard-map` (10), `capability-gates` (9), `project-overview` (9), `tool-rail-adapter` (6).

`pnpm typecheck` passes across all 36 packages. `pnpm check:workspace-registries` validates all 13 registries.

## Performance effect

Bundle grows 227.40 → 228.26 kB (+0.9 kB, +0.3 kB gzipped) for the whole workspace shell. Only the small runtime registries are imported; the icon, component and surface inventories (~280 kB of specification text) are read from disk by the validation script instead, never bundled.

CSS goes 0 → 2.78 kB because the shell stylesheet was previously never loaded at all.

## Accessibility effect

Net improvement, and the main reason several decisions went the way they did:

- The tab strip is a proper WAI-ARIA `tablist` with roving tabindex, so a keyboard user reaches the canvas without tabbing through every open view. Arrow keys move between tabs and wrap.
- Close controls are real nested `<button>`s, not hover-only affordances. Non-closeable tabs render no close control rather than a permanently dead disabled one.
- Every disabled tool and unavailable mode puts its reason in the **accessible name**, not only a `title` — a tooltip is unreachable by keyboard and by touch.
- Keyboard shortcuts never fire during IME composition, and never steal a keystroke a text field owns, with Escape the deliberate exception so a user can leave a field they did not mean to enter. Shortcut labels are platform-adapted; a Windows user is never shown `⌘`.
- The 44px touch minimum is preserved on coarse pointers. It is relaxed to doc 36's 36–40px desktop hitbox under `(pointer: fine)` only — a 44px control cannot fit a 40px tab strip, and both numbers are correct for their own input.
- Status is never colour-only; counts and states are written as words.

## Project format and migration effect

None. `@arq/workspace` cannot reach the model or the operation log, holds no async work, and performs no I/O. No schema, no migration, no `.arq` surface touched.

## Dependency and licence effect

None. No new third-party dependencies. Two new internal workspace links (`@arq/design-system` → `@arq/workspace`, `@arq/web` → `@arq/workspace`), reflected in `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

## Security and privacy effect

None. No network, storage or credential surface. The capability gates are conservative by construction: every gate defaults off except the one path with tested backing, so a surface cannot present a capability that has no system behind it.

## Rollback

The workspace work is self-contained in commit 1 and revertable on its own. `packages/workspace/` and `packages/design-system/src/workspace/` are new; the edits to existing shell components are additive (`ToolRail` gains an optional category and an optional per-tool field, `TopBar`/`StatusBar` gain `flex-wrap`, `ModelPanel`/`InspectorShell` drop hardcoded widths in favour of their dock).

Commit 3 is independently revertable and touches no behaviour.

### Note on commit 3

`pnpm format:check` was **already failing on the base branch**, on 97 files, none related to this work. It is the second step of `lint-and-typecheck`, so `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and the new registry gate never ran — nothing on this branch was being verified in CI. Two distinct problems were behind it:

- The repository had **no `.prettierignore`**, so Prettier was trying to restyle 19 generated files, including `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the timestamped benchmark result JSONs. That is churn by construction: pnpm rewrites the lockfile on the next install, and the benchmark files are recorded measurements. Now ignored.
- The remaining 64 are ordinary source files with genuine drift; `pnpm format` applied. Quote style, trailing commas and wrapping only.

Separately: `pnpm test` is still not a CI job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so the 1641 tests remain ungated on pull requests. Pre-existing, and left alone rather than changed unasked — worth a follow-up.

title: Harden .arq foundation, wire real file-open UI, add CI test gates (Phases 1-8 slice)
body:
## Problem

`packages/arqfs` accepted untrusted `.arq` files with no enforced storage bounds, no durable write boundary, and no way to promote a migrated file into place safely. `apps/web` had no file-open path at all, so the preflight logic that existed was never called. And CI never ran the test suite — every test in the repository had zero enforcement.

## Solution

12 commits. Each commit message carries its own full problem/solution/evidence writeup; `git log` on this branch is the detailed record.

**Storage layer (Phases 1–4)**
1. `3d808d5` Harden `.arq` safety foundation (ARQFS-001..004, 007, 008) — storage policy, byte preflight, resource integrity, durable local writes, safe mode, resource GC, Worker RPC transport.
2. `5273779` Prove migration/swap/export durability (ARQFS-005, 006, 011) — atomic swap with backup + rollback, migration cleanup, golden-fixture proof that migration preserves source bytes *and* semantic hash.
3. `2d6bcc6` Fix cross-project OPFS collision + Worker crash handling (ARQFS-008, 009).
4. `da3988d` Commit reviewed imports atomically (ARQFS-012, 013, 014) — zero partial canonical mutation on failure.

**UI (Phases 5–6)**
5. `4fbb64b` React Aria overlay foundation (UI-001, UI-003) — real focus-trapped dialog.
6. `367db80` Wire the byte-safe file-open gate into `apps/web` (UI-011).

**Observability + release gates (Phase 8)**
7. `71ce1d0` Lifecycle events, opt-in support bundle, and CI `test` + `browser-capability-checks` jobs (ARQFS-018, 020).

**CI fixes** — `8c37beb` portable Chromium path (the capability scripts hardcoded a sandbox-only path and had never run outside it); `e693d59` pre-existing prettier drift on 86 files.

**Self-critique fixes** — `5a13a78`, `6d2b2eb`, `21bc4c5`, described below.

## Defects found and fixed

Some in pre-existing code, some in this branch's own new code. Every one was confirmed by a probe before being called a bug, and re-verified by reverting the fix afterwards.

| # | Defect | Found in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `checkArqfsIntegrity` read a fixed `integrity_check` column, but `PRAGMA quick_check` names its column `quick_check` — so **every** file, healthy or corrupt, reported `ok: false`. | pre-existing |
| 2 | Content-addressed dedupe treated chunk layout as identity, rejecting legitimate re-stores (including every zero-length resource). | ported code |
| 3 | Every project opened through **one fixed OPFS filename** — OPFS is shared per origin, so two projects silently read/wrote the same database. Reproduced as real cross-contamination in headless Chromium before fixing. | pre-existing |
| 4 | `shell-controls.css` was never imported anywhere — every shell button rendered unstyled. Invisible to typecheck and unit tests, which render nothing. | pre-existing |
| 5 | `commitStagedImport` returned `committed` against a **non-existent session** (silent SQLite no-op). Only failed loudly when `issues` was non-empty, so the clean-import case was the silent one. | this branch |
| 6 | Provenance records could be **false about their own resource** — a probe stored `sha256:aaaa…`/`999999 bytes` against a real 16-byte resource. | this branch |
| 7 | Resource GC listed preserved import sources as orphaned, then hit their FK and **rejected the entire batch** — one protected resource blocked all cleanup permanently. | this branch |
| 8 | `FileOpenPanel` violated **WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name (A)** — accessible name did not contain the visible text, so voice control could not activate it. Mouse and keyboard both worked, which is why nothing caught it. | this branch |
| 9 | Top bar hard-coded `saveState="saved"` / `syncState="synced"` with no save pipeline and no sync backend — permanent false claims, against the repo's own "local save must never be represented as cloud success" rule. | pre-existing |

## Tests

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm typecheck` (35 workspace packages) | pass |
| `pnpm test` | **217 files / 1634 tests pass** |
| `pnpm format:check` | pass repo-wide |
| CI (all 8 checks on `21bc4c5`) | green |

Baseline before this branch was 17 files / 86 tests in `packages/arqfs`. Real headless-Chromium capability checks (OPFS persistence, writer-lock coordination, cross-project isolation, dialog focus trap + WCAG label-in-name, file-open preflight against real truncated/valid/non-Arq fixtures) are committed under `benchmarks/results/` with their scripts in `scripts/`, and now run on every PR.

## Reviewability caveat

The execution package asked for small PRs, one per coherent issue. This is one large PR (142 files) because GitHub's PR-creation endpoint returned HTTP 500 for most of the session, so work continued as separate commits on one branch. **The commits are individually reviewable and each is self-contained** — reviewing commit-by-commit is strongly preferable to reviewing the squashed diff.

Note also that `e693d59` (prettier drift) touches ~63 files unrelated to the feature work. It is formatting-only — verified token-identical on spot-checked files — and is isolated to that one commit if you would rather split it out.

## Project format and migration effect

**No schema change.** No table, column or `user_version` altered; existing `.arq` files are unaffected on disk.

Behaviour at the open boundary is deliberately stricter: future-major, future-schema, truncated, or unreadable-feature-flag files are now refused into editable mode. Copy-on-write migration is preserved and strengthened — the source is still never mutated, and the target must now also pass an integrity check before success is reported.

## Security and privacy effect

Net positive. Path traversal, drive-letter and control-character paths rejected; entry/archive/resource/chunk sizes bounded; truncated and header-inconsistent SQLite files rejected before use. Telemetry added in `71ce1d0` carries only stable codes, counts, durations and versions — never a filename, path, project name or raw driver message — enforced at runtime by a denylist check, with an opt-in-only support bundle that has no automatic call site.

## Known blockers / non-goals

- **Phase 7 (typed operation envelope + sync protocol) not attempted.** ADR-0019 and ADR-0021 are both still `Proposed` and are 52–78 word stubs; the repo's own rules forbid introducing a schema/operation-journal/sync protocol without an accepted ADR. This needs an owner decision, not more code.
- **UI-002, UI-004–010, UI-012–019 not attempted.** The 84-component / 57-surface scope needs per-component design and accessibility review with human-reviewed visual baselines. Two components were done properly rather than 84 superficially.
- **ARQFS-019 device lab out of scope** — only headless Chromium was available; no Safari, Firefox or physical devices.
- **One contradiction deliberately left visible:** the shell still renders a hard-coded demo model tree beside "No project open". The sample data is the fake there, not the honest status label — whether the demo shell keeps showing it is a product decision, not something to resolve by restoring the false "Saved".

## Rollback

Each commit reverts independently. One caveat: reverting `3d808d5` restores the broken `checkArqfsIntegrity`, which reports every file as failing its integrity check — keep that fix even in a partial rollback.

title: ARQFS-001: Make `.arq` open a byte-safe compatibility gate
body:
## Problem

The file picker must not hand arbitrary or future `.arq` bytes to SQLite or the editor. A reader must distinguish malformed, incompatible and healthy files before authoring begins.

## Scope

- Wire `preflightArqfsBytes` into every file-open path.
- Validate SQLite header fields, page/file limits, ARQ application ID, frozen meta, schema and required feature flags.
- Return stable reason codes and route to editable, read-only, migration or blocked states.

## Acceptance criteria

- Truncated, oversized, wrong-ID, future-major, future-schema and unknown-required-feature fixtures never construct an editable session.
- Older same-major schemas offer copy-on-write migration.
- The UI shows a short actionable message plus a diagnostics affordance.
- No raw SQLite error or empty editor shell leaks to users.

Scenarios: S001–S017.

## Live implementation status (2026-07-24)

The storage-layer half of this issue has landed on `claude/arq-master-agent-execution-ir9re1` (commit `3d808d5`):

- `packages/arqfs/src/arqfs-preflight.ts` — raw SQLite header checks for journal mode, reserved bytes, payload fractions, application ID, and declared vs physical page count (truncation detection), each with a stable code (`ARQ_INVALID_JOURNAL_MODE`, `ARQ_INVALID_RESERVED_BYTES`, `ARQ_INVALID_PAYLOAD_FRACTIONS`, `ARQ_FILE_TRUNCATED`, `ARQ_PAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`).
- `packages/arqfs/src/arqfs-open.ts` — refuses future-major and future-schema files, requires numeric version metadata, and treats unreadable feature flags as structural failure rather than "no flags declared".

Evidence: `npx vitest run packages/arqfs --coverage=false` → 23 files / 121 tests pass against a real `better-sqlite3` binding.

### Remaining for this issue

The **UI half is not done**: no file-open path is wired to `preflightArqfsBytes` yet, and no user-facing message or diagnostics affordance exists. That work depends on UI-011 (file open / import UI) and is tracked there.

Dependencies: UI-011, UI-013.

title: reliability: import-export worker cancellation has a race with in-flight conversion
body:
Fixed in d19d388.

**Bug (FP-019):** `workers/import-export-worker/src/handler.ts` adapters only check `AbortSignal.aborted` once, at the very start of `convert()`. If a `cancel` request arrived after that check but before `convert()` resolved, the handler would still post a final `'converted'`/`'failed'` message for a request the caller had already been told was `'cancelled'` — a real race, not hypothetical, since today's adapters do all their work inside one synchronous-looking `async` call with no later checkpoint.

**Fix:** added a `cancelledRequestIds: Set<string>` plus a `postFinal()` wrapper that silently drops any late `'converted'`/`'failed'` post for a requestId already reported as `'cancelled'`. Once a request is cancelled its outcome is permanently `'cancelled'`; anything settling afterward is dropped, not posted.

**Regression test:** new test in `handler.test.ts` uses a fake adapter whose `convert()` only resolves when the test explicitly releases it, so the cancel genuinely arrives mid-flight (not just asserting the code path exists). Asserts `post` is called exactly once, with `{ type: 'cancelled', requestId: 'r5' }`, and never with `'converted'` or `'failed'`.

Verified: `npx vitest run workers/import-export-worker` — 6/6 passing. `npx turbo run typecheck --filter=@arq/import-export-worker` — clean.

title: Rebuild README with canonical brand wordmark and honest status
body:
## Problem

The root `README.md` was stale and inaccurate: it claimed "no product code has shipped yet" while the repository already contains a working app shell, design system, Rust/WASM core, storage prototypes, and a full test/benchmark suite. It also used a plain-text logo instead of the canonical ARQ brand wordmark, had no light/dark handling, no honest split between working code and roadmap items, and an architecture diagram that didn't distinguish shipped systems from staged/future ones.

## Solution

Replaced `README.md` with a rebuilt version:

- Canonical ARQ SVG wordmark (`brand/01_VECTOR/`) with Phthalo Green (light mode) / white (dark mode) variants via `<picture>` + `prefers-color-scheme`.
- Brand-consistent badges and a clearer first screen with an immediate pre-release warning.
- A status table separating working code, prototypes, active validation, and deferred roadmap items — no invented functionality or premature product claims.
- An architecture diagram (Mermaid) with staged/later systems shown on dashed connections, distinct from shipped systems.
- Corrected `.arq`, SQLite, OPFS, Rust, WebAssembly, React, and TypeScript descriptions, described as implementation direction under validation rather than a finished guarantee.
- Exact install, build, test, benchmark, Rust, and licence-check commands, verified against the current root `package.json` scripts.
- An accurate repository map matching the current top-level layout.
- A complete logo/brand implementation section (canonical asset locations, colours, minimum sizes, prohibited logo changes, and a pointer to the shared `Logo` component).
- AI boundary, security, professional-use, contribution, and proprietary licence sections.
- No em dashes, no inconsistent casing, no screenshot of the current hardcoded demo scene presented as a finished product.

All linked paths (`brand/01_VECTOR/*.svg`, `brand/00_GUIDE/*.pdf`, `docs/adr/`, `docs/product/ARQ-COMPLETE-PRODUCT-ENGINEERING-BLUEPRINT-v1.0.md`, `docs/architecture/REPOSITORY-STRUCTURE.md`, `packages/design-system/src/logo.tsx`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`) and every `pnpm` command referenced were checked against the current repository tree and `package.json` before merging in this change.

## Non-goals

This PR only touches `README.md`. It does not fix the following repository-level issues, which were identified during this review and need separate follow-up:

1. `NOTICE` still says the repository has no third-party code and contains planning documentation only, which is no longer accurate now that implementation dependencies are present.
2. `LICENSE` still contains a placeholder for the legal copyright holder.
3. The active product blueprint's own header still calls itself "Proposed" and says it takes control only "once approved," while the rest of the docs treat it as the current source of truth.
4. The repository's default branch is a temporary `claude/*` branch rather than a stable, protected branch such as `main`.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable — text/markdown change only, using existing brand assets already committed to the repository (`brand/01_VECTOR/`).

## Tests

Not applicable — documentation-only change. No code, scripts, or dependencies were modified.

## Performance effect

None.

## Accessibility effect

None. Wordmark and symbol images retain descriptive `alt` text.

## Project format and migration effect

None.

## Dependency and licence effect

None.

## Security and privacy effect

None.

## Rollback

Revert this commit; no schema, dependency, or code changes are involved.

body:
Bumps [better-sqlite3](https://github.com/WiseLibs/better-sqlite3) from 11.10.0 to 13.0.1.
Release notes

Sourced from better-sqlite3's releases.

v13.0.1

Full Changelog: https://github.com/WiseLibs/better-sqlite3/compare/v13.0.0...v13.0.1

Fixed a regression in parameter binding where it would be overly strict and reject plain objects from other realms (e.g., in jest tests).

v13.0.0

Version 13.0.0 marks a major milestone, as it's the first version of better-sqlite3 to run on the N-API. This means prebuilt binaries should theoretically work across different versions of Node.js and Electron, and perhaps even other runtimes like Bun. As a result, we've removed the deprecated prebuild-install dependency, and now prebuilt binaries are published directly with the better-sqlite3 code itself. If your platform/architecture doesn't have a prebuilt binary, it should compile during install as before.

What's Changed

  • Refactored codebase to use node-addon-api by @​JoshuaWise in WiseLibs/better-sqlite3#1498
  • Added a new db.explain() method, for running EXPLAIN queries without needing to supply bound parameters.
  • Added a new preparedStatement.toString() method, for getting the expanded SQL of a prepared statement.
  • Fix SqliteError cross-realm and Error.isError compatibility by @​dennismutuku2005 in WiseLibs/better-sqlite3#1473

Direct Uploads

title: sync: implement safe rebase and conflict classes
body:
**ARQ-209** | Phase: File-system and instant architecture foundation

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/209-sync-implement-safe-rebase-and-conflict-classes.md`

## Resolution

Commit `998906e` adds `conflict-classification.ts` + `safe-rebase.ts`. Operations are described only by which entity IDs they wrote/deleted (not their full semantic type), keeping this package decoupled from `@arq/operations`/`@arq/arqscript` - a real, standard optimistic-concurrency conflict-detection pattern (compare touched-entity sets), not a placeholder.

`classifyConflict` distinguishes `concurrent-write` (both wrote the same entity - mergeable in principle) from the more severe `write-after-delete` (one deleted an entity the other wrote to). `computeSafeRebasePlan` classifies each client operation independently against the server operations since its `baseRevision` - a conflicted operation is reported explicitly with its conflict class and the specific conflicting server operation, never silently reapplied or dropped, matching "invalid operations leave committed state unchanged."

**Explicit scope boundary, documented rather than silently assumed away**: no transitive dependency-chain analysis between a client's own pending operations (e.g. operation B assumed operation A's effect, A conflicted, so B might now be unsafe too even though B itself touches nothing server-side changed) - that needs real operation semantics this generic module does not have.

13 new tests across both modules. Full monorepo: 31/31 packages typecheck, 167/167 test files (1298 tests) pass.

title: sync: implement resumable resource chunk upload
body:
**ARQ-208** | Phase: File-system and instant architecture foundation

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/208-sync-implement-resumable-resource-chunk-upload.md`

## Resolution

Commit `998906e` adds `createChunkUploadSession`, built directly on `@arq/arqfs`'s content-addressed chunks (ARQ-199) - each chunk already carries its own sha256, which is exactly what a real resumable-upload negotiation needs. A resuming client asks which chunk indices are still missing (`missingChunkIndices()`) and sends only those, not the whole resource again. A chunk re-sent at an already-accepted index with the same hash is a safe duplicate; with a **different** hash it is rejected rather than silently overwriting a verified chunk.

7 new tests, including the actual resume scenario (partial upload, connection drop, missing-index query). Full monorepo: 31/31 packages typecheck, 167/167 test files (1298 tests) pass.

title: security: configure SQLite defensive open policy
body:
**ARQ-237** | Epic: v3 execution readiness

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/237-security-configure-sqlite-defensive-open-policy.md`

## Resolution

Commit `2cd4ebb` adds `arqfs-defensive-open.ts`: `applyDefensiveOpenPolicy(driver, { readOnly })` sets `PRAGMA trusted_schema = OFF` (disables trusted-schema-only SQL functions/features a malicious file's embedded triggers/views/check-constraints could otherwise invoke), a bounded `busy_timeout` (5000ms, rather than indefinite blocking on lock contention), and `PRAGMA query_only = ON` for read-only opens (pairs with `resolveArqfsSafeModePlan`'s `openReadOnly`).

Every claim verified directly against this exact driver, not assumed from SQLite's documentation: `trusted_schema` actually reads back `0` after being set; a write under `query_only=ON` actually throws (`attempt to write a readonly database`); and separately, `load_extension()` as a SQL function is confirmed rejected by SQLite's own default build (`not authorized`) - checked directly rather than assumed - and this codebase never calls the driver-level `loadExtension()` API either, so no untrusted file content can reach extension loading through either path.

5 new tests. Full monorepo: 30/30 packages typecheck, 162/162 test files (1267 tests) pass.

body:
**ARQ-222** | Epic: v3 execution readiness

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/222-file-system-implement-canonical-semantic-hashing-test-oracle.md`

## Resolution

Commit `2cd4ebb` adds `arqfs-semantic-hash.ts`: `computeProjectSemanticHash` is SHA-256 over every archive entry, in canonical (sorted-path) order, each length-prefixed rather than NUL-separated - a path/content pair split at the same byte offset under a naive separator scheme cannot collide with a different split (verified directly with exactly that adversarial case: `{path:'ab',content:'c'}` vs `{path:'a',content:'bc'}` hash differently).

Also verifies determinism regardless of insertion order (canonical ordering, not insertion order) and that any single-byte content change changes the hash.

title: security: fuzz untrusted arq reader and migrations
body:
**ARQ-217** | Phase: File-system and instant architecture foundation

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/217-security-fuzz-untrusted-arq-reader-and-migrations.md`

## Resolution

Commit `2cd4ebb` adds `arqfs-fuzz.test.ts`: property-based fuzzing (`fast-check`, 200+ runs for the reader, 100+ for archive entries, 50+ for resource chunks and migrations) of `openArqfs`, `putArchiveEntry`/`getArchiveEntry`, `putResource`/`assembleResource`, and `migrateArqfsCopyOnWrite` against arbitrary/random input.

**Found two real bugs, both fixed, transparently disclosed rather than silently absorbed:**
1. The fuzz test itself had an unawaited `fc.assert(fc.asyncProperty(...))`, letting Vitest's `afterEach` close the driver mid-run and produce a confusing "database connection is not open" error unrelated to the actual property being tested. Fixed by properly awaiting it - a real async-test mistake worth calling out, not a library bug.
2. Once fixed, fuzzing immediately found a real defect: `putResource` threw a `UNIQUE constraint failed` error when storing content whose sha256 already existed, rather than treating it as the idempotent no-op content-addressed storage requires (identical bytes hash identically, so re-storing them must be safe, not a conflict). Fixed with an existence check before insert in the same transaction, plus a dedicated named regression test (`arqfs-resource-chunks.test.ts`) so this doesn't rely solely on the fuzz test catching it again.

Full monorepo: 30/30 packages typecheck, 162/162 test files (1267 tests) pass, fuzz suite re-run multiple times with different random seeds for stability.

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/201-file-system-implement-copy-on-write-migrations.md`

Commit `e4bd4f1` adds `packages/arqfs/src/arqfs-migration.ts`. Built on ARQ-197's `VACUUM INTO`: the source is only ever read from, never mutated. A migration transform applies to a fresh copy, which is then verified (reopened, checked against `openArqfs`) before this function reports success.

body:
**ARQ-225** | Phase: File-system and instant architecture foundation

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/225-core-implement-deterministic-record-ordering.md`

Commit `e4bd4f1` adds `rust/arq-core/src/ordering.rs`: `canonical_sort_ids` sorts stable IDs by byte-wise UTF-8 comparison. title: file-system: implement content addressed resource chunks
body:
**ARQ-199** | Phase: File-system and instant architecture foundation

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/199-file-system-implement-content-addressed-resource-chunks.md`

## Resolution

Commit `0b2152f` adds `packages/arqfs/src/arqfs-resource-chunks.ts` and a new `resource_chunk` table (the `resource` table from ARQ-195 only had the descriptor shape, no actual chunk storage). `putResource` splits whole content into chunks (each with its own sha256) and stores the descriptor + every chunk in one transaction; `assembleResource` reassembles them, re-verifying every chunk's hash and the total byte length against the descriptor rather than trusting storage - never throws, reports any inconsistency as a `rejected` result.

Tested against real corruption scenarios, not just the happy path: a tampered chunk (hash mismatch) and a missing chunk row are both caught and rejected with a specific reason. A zero-length resource deliberately still gets exactly one (empty) chunk rather than zero, so the chunk-count check always has something to check against.

title: architecture: remove active storage and archive contradictions
body:
## Correction to the previous close

The first pass (commit `5243d75`) only fixed the storage-tier half of this issue's
title ("active storage" - Dexie vs SQLite). It missed the "archive" half: `@arq/project-format`
already defines a *different* `.arq` container - a zip-shaped logical archive
(`manifest.json`/`model.json`/`operations.ndjson`/`views.json`/`sheets.json`/
`checksums.json`, ARQ-076 through ARQ-080, with its own migration registry) - which
ADR-0019's SQLite format would otherwise silently collide with under the same ".arq"
name. Reopening rather than leaving that gap under a closed issue.

Commit `4c43b4a` resolves it: both containers stay valid, for different purposes. The
new SQLite file (ADR-0019) becomes the live, working, user-visible project file;
`@arq/project-format`'s existing zip-of-files archive remains the portable
export/interchange format, unchanged. `packages/arqfs` (ARQ-195) will store
`@arq/project-format`'s existing entries as SQLite rows/blobs - it does not
reimplement manifest parsing, checksums, or migration sequencing, all of which stay
exactly where they are. See `docs/architecture/ARQ-FILE-FORMAT.md`'s new
"Relationship to the existing `@arq/project-format` archive" section and
`docs/product/DECISION-REGISTER.csv` D-023.

Re-closing now that both halves of the title are actually addressed.

title: Make Zeus echo the real per-prompt contract, not a generic reminder
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #224 (merged). After Zeus was wired in, the `UserPromptSubmit` hook (`scripts/zeus-hook.sh`) printed the exact same static one-line reminder — `[ZEUS 4 INTERNAL] Load FAST-KERNEL only; route modules; ...` — on every single actionable prompt, regardless of what the prompt actually was. It was visible in the transcript, but useless as visibility: it never showed what Zeus actually decided for that specific prompt (classification, routing, acceptance criteria), so there was no way to see "the updated prompt" Zeus produced.

## Solution

The hook now runs the real compiler (`node scripts/zeus-fast-compile.mjs --task "<the prompt>"`) and echoes its actual markdown output back into the conversation for every actionable prompt: mode / risk / tier / delivery stop, owner and reviewers, routed modules, acceptance criteria, and checks. Falls back to the old static line only if the compile step itself fails (e.g. `node` unavailable), so the hook can never go silently broken.

Updated `CLAUDE.md`'s description of the hook to match the real behavior, and updated `test-zeus-hook.sh`'s assertion to check for the new output signature (`Zeus 4 Compact Contract`) instead of the old static string.

## Non-goals

- No change to the classification/routing logic itself (`scripts/lib/zeus-engine.mjs`) — only to what the hook surfaces.
- No change to acknowledgement/`/zeus-*`/webhook silencing — verified those still produce no output.
- No application code changes.

## Visual evidence

N/A — this is a CLI/hook text-output change, not a UI change. Example of new output for an actionable prompt:

```
Zeus 4 routed this prompt:
# Zeus 4 Compact Contract

**Mode / risk / tier / stop:** implement / moderate / standard / local-green
**Owner:** geometry-bim
**Modules:** geometry, arqfs

**Acceptance**
- [ ] authoritative current state inspected
- [ ] requested success and failure paths work
- [ ] applicable Arq invariants remain satisfied
- [ ] local-green has current evidence
- [ ] integrity, recovery and source-preservation evidence passes

**Checks**
- ranked context retrieval
- impact-selected focused checks
- actual output inspection
- affected package quality checks
- independent critique pass
```

## Tests

- `bash scripts/test-zeus-hook.sh` → passes with the updated assertion.
- `bash scripts/test-zeus-system.sh` (from source package) → full suite passes.
- Manually piped fast/standard/deep-tier prompts through the hook and confirmed each produces its own distinct, accurate contract (different owner/modules/checks per tier and risk).
- Manually confirmed `ok`, `/zeus-audit ...`, and webhook/task-notification payloads still produce no output.
- `node scripts/zeus.mjs verify` and `node scripts/zeus.mjs benchmark --root .` still green.

## Performance effect

Adds one `node` process invocation (the compiler) per actionable prompt inside the hook. Measured compile step is sub-millisecond in-process; the dominant cost is Node startup (tens of ms), which is negligible for a once-per-prompt hook.

## Accessibility effect

None.

## Project format and migration effect

None.

## Dependency and licence effect

None.

## Security and privacy effect

None — the compiler only reads the prompt text already available to the hook and repo-local config; no new external calls.

## Rollback

Revert this commit; the hook falls back to the prior static-reminder behavior.

title: Install Zeus 4.0 prompt operating system
body:
## Problem

Arq had no structured prompt-operating layer for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex/AGENTS). Ad hoc prompting risks assumption-driven changes to protected areas: semantic BIM model integrity, `.arq` file/migration safety, renderer independence, geometry correctness, sync, and accessibility.

## Solution

Installs the Zeus 4.0 Instant Execution System, a silent-first prompt operating system built around a small Fast Kernel (`.zeus/FAST-KERNEL.md`):

- Classifies requests into fast/standard/deep execution tiers by risk and scope, routing to at most 1/4/8 domain modules under `.zeus/modules/` (geometry, arqfs, security, ui-visual, rendering, accessibility, ai, architecture, interoperability, github-cicd, incident, release-production).
- Builds an incremental, gitignored project index (`.zeus/cache/`) for ranked context retrieval instead of reading whole files/repo by default.
- Runs an adaptive check ladder (focused → affected package → repository gate → CI → deployment → production) via a unified CLI, `scripts/zeus.mjs` (compile/route/index/context/impact/check/status/release/benchmark/verify).
- Wires into Claude Code (`.claude/`), Cursor (`.cursor/`), Codex/generic agents (`AGENTS.md`), and GitHub Copilot (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`).
- Ships an installer/uninstaller, hook tests, prompt-compiler self-tests, architecture/security lint fixtures, and an evaluation recorder.

Installed via the package's own `scripts/install-zeus.sh`, which is purely additive here — no existing repository files were overwritten (verified: no filename collisions with existing `docs/`, `scripts/`, or `examples/` content, and `AGENTS.md`/root `README.md` did not previously exist or were not touched).

## Non-goals

- Does not change any Arq application code, build, or runtime behavior.
- Does not perform any GitHub write beyond this PR (merge/deploy tooling is included but reports `blocked` rather than fabricating success, since no `gh` CLI/authorization is available in this environment).
- Does not modify the existing `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, or any pre-existing `docs/`, `scripts/`, or `examples/` files.

## Visual evidence

N/A — no UI change; this is prompt/documentation/tooling only.

## Tests

- `node scripts/zeus.mjs verify` → "Zeus 4 verification passed (14 required files)."
- `bash scripts/test-zeus-system.sh` (run from the source package, where the `quality/` self-test fixtures live — those fixtures are dev-only and intentionally not installed into the target repo) → "Zeus 4 full system tests passed."
- `node scripts/zeus.mjs benchmark --root .` against this repo → `"status": "green"` (compile/route p95 0.049ms, fresh index 188ms, cache-hit context query 103ms — all under configured targets).
- `node scripts/zeus.mjs index` → built a project index over 984 tracked files.
- `node scripts/zeus.mjs status` → honestly reports `"blocked"` ("gh CLI unavailable") rather than claiming a GitHub write succeeded.

## Performance effect

None on the application. Zeus's own overhead (measured against this repo): compile/route p50 ~0.014ms/p95 ~0.05ms, fresh project index ~189ms, cached index lookup ~177ms — all well under the package's own budget targets.

## Accessibility effect

None — no application UI touched. The included `ui-visual` module encodes accessibility/pixel-precision requirements for future agent-driven UI work.

## Project format and migration effect

None — no changes to `.arq` format, schema, or migration code.

## Dependency and licence effect

No new runtime dependencies. Adds Node scripts (using only built-ins) under `scripts/`.

## Security and privacy effect

No secrets or tokens included. `.zeus/cache/` (project index/lock files) is gitignored via `.zeus/.gitignore`. The system's own docs (`docs/SECURITY-THREAT-MODEL.md`, `.zeus/modules/security.md`) define an untrusted-content/prompt-injection boundary for future agent use.

## Rollback

`bash scripts/uninstall-zeus.sh /path/to/Arq` removes only the files recorded in `.zeus/install-manifest.jsonl` (Zeus-owned files from this install), or simply revert this PR's commit.

title: editor: implement centre and nearest snap
body:
**ARQ-191** | Phase: Phase 1 | Epic: Editor interaction | Priority: high | Dependencies: ARQ-052, ARQ-192

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals: `backlog/issues/191-editor-implement-centre-and-nearest-snap.md`

## Resolution

Nearest snap was already done (see prior comment - `nearest-snap.ts`, commit be68b6f). Commit [`0c35b83`](https://github.com/ruddvz/Arq/commit/0c35b83) completes the Centre half:

- Split the missing closed-shape candidate contract into its own issue, ARQ-192 (`backlog/issues/192-editor-define-circular-snap-candidate.md`), per this issue's own non-goal against inventing an unfounded circle/arc type inline.

title: ipad: prototype RoomPlan conversion
body:
**ARQ-173** | Phase: Phase 8 | Epic: Native iPad | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-172

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/173-ipad-prototype-roomplan-conversion.md`

## Resolution

Commit `3801600` adds a new `@arq/roomplan-adapter` package implementing the buildable half of blueprint section 109's 11-step RoomPlan conversion pipeline — `docs/research/ROOMPLAN-CONVERSION.md` has the full step-by-step table.

- **Implemented**: confidence preserved per element; unit and coordinate check (metres → millimetres); convert to Arq operations (one `@arq/arqscript` `CreateWall`/`PlaceDoor`/`PlaceWindow` command per captured element); show uncertainty (`lowConfidenceElementIds`, never hidden); retain source scan provenance (`scanObjectId`, RoomPlan's own stable identifier).
- **Real bug caught and fixed before shipping**: the first version passed captured metre coordinates straight through, but `createWallCommand` rejects negative coordinates while RoomPlan/ARKit's world-space origin is wherever the device started scanning — real captures are routinely negative. Fixed by translating every wall point to the room's own bounding-box minimum before conversion (`findMinimumCorner`), covered by a dedicated test with negative captured coordinates, and the applied origin is kept visible on the result (`originMeters`) rather than applied invisibly.
- **Honestly scoped out**: simplify, resolve intersections, and validate rooms (steps 5, 6, 10) need real geometry infrastructure applied to a whole converted project — larger scope than single-element conversion, and better validated against real captured data than synthetic numbers. Capture itself (step 1) needs real LiDAR hardware and the native RoomPlan/ARKit framework, neither available in this sandboxed environment. No accuracy claim is made anywhere, matching section 109's own "do not call it survey-grade by default."
- **Never silently drops a captured element**: a malformed element (e.g. an opening naming an empty host wall id) is recorded in `failedElements`, never thrown past the converter, and never blocks the rest of the room from converting.
- **This epic's shared acceptance criteria** ("Pencil, finger and keyboard roles are separated", "native value compared with browser behaviour") don't materially apply here — RoomPlan conversion has no pointer-input surface; noted explicitly in the README rather than forced.

## Evidence

- 9 new tests: full wall+door+window conversion, negative-coordinate translation, low/high confidence reporting, a failed element not blocking the rest, empty-room handling, and provenance linkage.
- Full workspace suite: 1195/1195 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean across all packages (`turbo run typecheck`, 28/28). Prettier clean.

Routed via the Zeus system (`node scripts/zeus.mjs route`). No new dependencies.

title: ipad: prototype native hover
body:
**ARQ-172** | Phase: Phase 8 | Epic: Native iPad | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-171

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/172-ipad-prototype-native-hover.md`

## Resolution

Commit `3389cc3` adds `hover-preview.ts` to `@arq/input-system`, building the actual hover-preview interaction on top of ARQ-171's confirmed `pointerover`-without-`pointerdown` capability.

- **Pencil, finger and keyboard roles are separated**: `createHoverPreviewTracker` only starts a hover session for a pointer `pointer-role.ts`'s `classifyPointerInputRole` reports as `'pencil'` — a `'touch'` or `'mouse'` `over` sample is correctly ignored (verified by test), matching blueprint section 13's assignment of "hover preview" to Apple Pencil specifically, not Finger or Keyboard/trackpad.
- **Native value compared with browser behaviour**: a second real-browser check (`hover-sequence-capability.html` + `run-hover-sequence-capability-check.mjs`, `pnpm benchmark:hover-sequence`) dispatched a full `over -> move -> move -> out` sequence (no `down`) for `pen`, `touch`, and `mouse` pointer types in real headless Chromium.
- **Honest, important finding recorded rather than glossed over**: all three pointer types produced an *identical* event sequence — the DOM's dispatch API does not restrict a hover sequence by `pointerType` at all. The Pencil-only restriction is entirely this repository's own application-level role check, not something the browser enforces. Separately, real touchscreens have no hardware hover/proximity sensing at all (a real finger physically cannot generate `pointerover` before contact the way a real Pencil can) — but confirming that physical difference needs real touch hardware, which this sandboxed environment does not have; only the synthetic-dispatch behavior was verified here. Documented explicitly in `docs/research/PENCIL-WEB-INPUT.md`, not hidden.
- A real contact (`pointerdown`) always ends the current hover-preview session for that pointer, matching how a real Pencil transitions from hovering to touching.

## Evidence

- 10 new tests (`hover-preview.test.ts`): session start/move/end, contact ending hover, touch/mouse correctly ignored, multiple concurrent pointers, and re-starting after a session ends.
- Real measured browser result (headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37), saved to `benchmarks/results/hover-sequence-capability-2026-07-23T19-10-01-385Z.json` and written up in `docs/research/PENCIL-WEB-INPUT.md`.
- Full workspace suite: 1186/1186 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean across all packages (`turbo run typecheck`, 27/27). Prettier clean.

Routed via the Zeus system (`node scripts/zeus.mjs route`). No new dependencies.
