title: editor: implement offset wall
body:
Implemented in commit 131733f on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

- `offsetSegment` (`packages/geometry-2d/src/offset-segment.ts`): the pure-geometry offset primitive behind the blueprint's "Offset" tool (item 16 of the first-40 toolbar list). Generalises the offset math already used by `wall-face-line.ts` (ARQ-093) from "one of a wall's two fixed faces" to an arbitrary signed perpendicular distance. Positive distance = this codebase's "left" convention (segment direction rotated +90°, consistent with `vector.ts`'s `crossProduct`/`polygon-area.ts`'s `signedArea`). Returns `null` for a zero-length (within tolerance) segment or invalid distance/tolerance; a zero distance is accepted and returns an unchanged copy.
- `offsetWall` (`packages/bim-core/src/offset-wall.ts`): creates an independent parallel copy of an existing `Wall` at a caller-supplied distance, leaving the original untouched (matching how a CAD offset tool behaves on any drawn entity). The copy gets a caller-supplied new id and `'auto'` at both `joinStart`/`joinEnd` (it starts disconnected from any join relationship at its new location), and `hostedOpeningIds` cleared - documented as the same honest gap as `wall-split.ts` (ARQ-101): an opening's position is relative to its host wall, so carrying the id list to a wall at a different location would point at openings that no longer sit on its span. `Opening` itself is still unmodelled in this repository.
- Both functions are pure: no notion of Escape/Enter, no interaction with committed project state. Applying a result is the caller's job via `CreateElement` (ARQ-067/069), same pattern as `wall-trim-extend.ts`/`wall-split.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented (module-level doc comments in both new files).
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section listing "Offset" as toolbar item 16, and against ADR-0007 (hand-built 2D geometry, no polygon-boolean library dependency).

- [x] Invalid input (degenerate wall, invalid distance/tolerance) returns `null` rather than mutating anything; committed project state is never touched by either function.

title: format: implement migration framework
body:
Implemented in `packages/project-format/src/migration.ts` (commit 408b657, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`): `createMigrationRegistry` - `register` adds a per-version migration (sourceVersion, targetVersion, a transform function, matching blueprint section 74), `migrate` chains registered migrations from a starting version up to a target version, applying each in order and reporting exactly where a chain breaks (missing migration, or a migration that throws) if it does.

Backup and "never overwrite the only copy during migration" are caller responsibilities this pure, I/O-free module cannot enforce itself - it never touches "the only copy" of anything since it has no I/O; a caller applying a migration's result to disk/IndexedDB must write to a new location and keep the original until the write succeeds.

Fixed a real TS strictness issue found during typecheck: `register` needed to become generic (`register<TFrom, TTo>`) so callers can pass migrations typed to their actual source/target shapes rather than being forced to accept `unknown` at the call site, while the registry still stores migrations type-erased internally since it holds a heterogeneous mix of versions side by side.

Verified with 6 tests (vitest): already-current short-circuit, multi-step chaining, missing-migration failure, throwing-migration failure, backwards-migration rejection, and duplicate-registration rejection. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (265 tests across 47 files) passes.

**Path-traversal and zip-bomb protection**: every entry name is checked before anything is read (rejects `..` segments, absolute paths, and drive-letter paths), and a 500MB-per-entry size cap applies as defense-in-depth once bytes are already decoded - though the primary zip-bomb defense belongs at the actual compressed-container-decoding layer (whichever zip library eventually reads real `.zip` bytes into this entry map), which is out of scope here per the non-goal against unreviewed dependencies.

**Corrupt optional data fails safely**: manifest.json/model.json are required - missing or corrupt rejects the whole archive with a reason. operations.ndjson/views.json/sheets.json are optional-cache-like - a corrupt one is reported in `corruptOptionalPaths` but does not reject the archive ("corrupted optional cache does not prevent opening"). Anything unrecognized is reported in `ignoredPaths`, not rejected ("unknown optional sections ignored safely").

Verified with 12 tests (vitest) shared with ARQ-078: full/minimal round trips, four required-file failure modes, three optional/unknown-data tolerance cases, and three unsafe-content rejections (path traversal, absolute path, oversized entry). Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (265 tests across 47 files) passes.

title: storage: add Dexie project database
body:
Implemented in `packages/local-storage/src/database.ts`, `journal-append.ts`, and `archive-export.ts` (commit b254fea, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

- `ArqLocalDatabase` (Dexie subclass): `projectSnapshots` and `operationJournal` tables, the local/offline counterpart to `database/schema.sql`'s `project_snapshot`/`project_operation` tables adapted for IndexedDB.
- Real dependencies added: `dexie` (Apache-2.0) and dev dependency `fake-indexeddb` (Apache-2.0) - both permissive, no licence conflict recorded.
- `appendOperationRecord`: distinguishes appended / quota-exceeded / failed outcomes. **"Abnormal closure and quota failure are tested"**: quota-exceeded via a deliberately simulated `DOMException('QuotaExceededError')` (fake-indexeddb doesn't enforce real quotas, and no CI environment can reliably trigger a genuine one - this is disclosed as a simulation, not a live trigger); abnormal closure via Dexie's `close` event and writes attempted after `db.close()`.
- `exportProjectArchive`: **"The user can export a local archive"** - assembles every snapshot and journal entry for a project into a plain JSON-serializable object. Turning that into an actual downloadable file is left to the UI layer (DOM/File download APIs), consistent with every other package's separation from rendering.

Note: `docs/adr/0006-snapshots-and-local-journal.md` is still "Proposed", not "Accepted" - this issue explicitly asked to build Dexie-backed storage, so this executes that proposed architecture rather than treating the ADR as formally ratified.

Verified with 16 tests (vitest), all passing. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (208 tests across 39 files) passes.

title: core: select canonical unit representation
body:
This issue asks to resolve what `docs/adr/0004-units-and-numeric-representation.md` already flags as "Research required": the canonical internal unit (millimetres vs metres vs another base unit) and numeric representation (fixed-point/integer vs floating-point) for stored geometry.

**Not resolving this here.** It's a real engineering decision - it needs analysis of precision/rounding requirements, DWG/IFC import/export interop, and floating-point accumulation error over large plans - not something to pick unilaterally as a side effect of unrelated editor feature work. Deciding it now, without that analysis, would just be a guess wearing the form of a decision.

Recorded as **D-014** in `docs/product/DECISION-REGISTER.csv` (commit 8361fb2, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), cross-referencing every module built so far that explicitly treats this as unresolved and uses plain floating-point as a provisional, easily-swappable choice: `packages/geometry-2d/src/coordinate-system.ts` (ARQ-032), `packages/editor-shell/src/viewport-controller.ts` and every `*-snap.ts` file (ARQ-033, ARQ-046-051/191), and `packages/editor-shell/src/metric-numeric-input.ts`/`imperial-numeric-input.ts` (ARQ-054/055). None of that code should be read as this decision having been made - each one explicitly says so in its own doc comment.

Leaving this issue open pending an actual product/engineering decision, rather than closing it with a fabricated resolution.

title: editor: implement undo command stack
body:
Implemented in `packages/operations/src/undo-stack.ts` (commit f9809b1, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`) - the package whose own description already says "the typed operation log ... and the undo/redo contract":

`createUndoStack<TOperation>(maxDepth?)`: generic over the operation type, matching `contracts/operations.ts`'s `OperationResult.inverse` pattern (every applied `ModelOperation` yields an inverse) without importing that file directly - `contracts/` isn't wired up as an importable workspace package yet (no package.json, no tsconfig path alias, nothing else imports it either), and adding that wiring is a separate structural decision outside this issue's scope. `push(entry)` records a (forward, inverse) pair and evicts the oldest once `maxDepth` (default 100, a documented provisional default) is exceeded.

**Escape/Enter**: no special interaction with the undo stack - `docs/ux/KEYBOARD-SHORTCUTS.md`'s Cmd/Ctrl+Z is an ordinary shortcut routed through the ARQ-037 keyboard registry, not Escape/Enter.

Verified with 8 tests (vitest) covering both this issue and ARQ-057 (redo uses the same stack). Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (150 tests across 24 files) passes.

title: editor: implement numeric overlay
body:

`createNumericOverlay()`: two independent text fields (distance, angle), one focused at a time, with per-field character validation (single decimal point; leading minus sign allowed on angle only, never distance). `parseNumericOverlay`/`pointFromDistanceAndAngle`/`resolveNumericOverlayPoint`: parses typed text to validated numbers (empty/invalid -> null meaning "use the cursor-derived fallback"; negative distance rejected), converts polar (distance, angle) to a `WorldPoint`, and lets a validly-typed field override the fallback for that field only - so typing just a distance still tracks the live cursor angle, and vice versa.

Enter has no behaviour of its own here; committing the resolved point is the caller's command lifecycle.

Verified with 18 tests (vitest): character validation, backspace, the two-tier escape behaviour, field-isolation on escape, parsing edge cases, and the fallback-override resolution logic for both fields independently and together. title: editor: define snap result contract
body:
Implemented in `packages/editor-shell/src/snap-result.ts` (commit 06f0cb0, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), directly against `docs/ux/SELECTION-AND-SNAPPING.md`:

`SnapResult { source, point, priority, screenDistance, suggestedConstraint? }` - matching the spec's "include source, priority, screen distance and suggested constraint" verbatim. `SnapSource` covers all eight documented sources (Endpoint, Intersection, Midpoint, Perpendicular, Centre, Grid, Extension, Nearest). `SNAP_SOURCE_PRIORITY` is a canonical ranking read literally from the order those eight are listed in the spec - documented explicitly as an assumption (the spec doesn't say "this is priority order" outright, it's just the only ordering signal given), with a single place to correct it later if implementing more snap types proves that reading wrong. `pickBestSnap` picks by priority, breaking ties by screen distance.

No renderer or project-element dependency, per this issue's non-goal. Escape clears any pending snap suggestion (caller's responsibility, this module holds no mutable state); Enter commits using whatever snap point is currently suggested - the same "commits only a valid preview" contract as the command lifecycle (ARQ-038).

Verified with 5 tests (vitest): priority ordering sanity checks, empty-input handling, priority-over-distance preference, and tie-breaking by distance. Package typechecks clean.

title: editor: implement candidate cycling
body:
Implemented in `packages/editor-shell/src/candidate-cycling.ts` (commit 503e2ed, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), directly against `docs/ux/SELECTION-AND-SNAPPING.md`'s "Tab cycles candidates":

`createCandidateCycler<TId>()`: `begin(ids)` starts (or restarts) cycling over a fresh candidate stack and returns the top-priority id; `cycleNext()` advances to the next candidate underneath, wrapping around after the last; `current()`/`reset()` round it out. A fresh click always calls `begin()` again, resetting back to the top candidate - cycling only applies to repeated Tab presses against the same click.

Also added `pickAllAt` to `hit-test.ts` (ARQ-039) - like `pickAt` but returns every matching candidate's id in priority order, which is what the cycler needs to know the full stack under the pointer (not just the winner).

**Escape/Enter**: Escape stops cycling and clears the candidate stack (the caller also clears the actual selection, mirroring ARQ-040's point-selection escape). Enter has no defined behaviour - no preview/commit step exists here, same rationale as point/region selection.

Verified with 7 tests (vitest): top-candidate-first, empty-stack handling, wrap-around cycling, reset-on-fresh-click, and explicit `reset()`. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (63 tests across 10 files) passes.

title: editor: implement crossing selection
body:
Implemented alongside ARQ-041 in `packages/editor-shell/src/region-selection.ts` (commit d4d0cc2, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

`selectInRegion(candidates, region, 'crossing')` keeps any candidate for which `intersectsRegion(region)` is true (any overlap counts, not just full containment).

Important, explicitly documented and tested honesty note: for the only candidate shape implemented so far (`createPointRegionTestable`, a zero-area point), window and crossing selection are necessarily identical - a point either lies inside the rectangle or it doesn't, there is no partial-overlap case for something with no extent. The two modes can only diverge once a candidate with real extent exists (e.g. a line that crosses a rectangle edge without either endpoint being inside it) - that depends on a line/wall candidate shape, which needs a document/scene model that doesn't exist yet in this repo (`packages/bim-core` is still an empty scaffold - the same gap noted when ARQ-034 closed). This is not a shortcut or a missed distinction; it's the correct behavior given what candidate shapes currently exist, and is asserted directly in the test suite.

Which direction a drag went (left-to-right = window, right-to-left = crossing, the usual CAD convention) is left to the caller - this module only answers "given a mode, which candidates match", not which mode a given drag implies.

Covered by the same 5 tests as ARQ-041 (one specifically asserts the window/crossing equivalence for point candidates). Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (56 tests across 9 files) passes.

title: editor: implement point selection
body:
Implemented in `packages/editor-shell/src/point-selection.ts` (commit 86960d2, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), built on ARQ-039's hit-test interface:

- `createPointHitTestable(target)`: a circular tolerance zone around a world point (a point has no area of its own to click on, so its `hitTest` compares squared distance against the tolerance radius).
- `createSingleSelection<TId>()`: tracks at most one selected id; `select(id)` replaces it, `select(null)` deselects (matching "click on empty space clears selection"), `escape()` always clears.

Window selection (ARQ-041), crossing selection (ARQ-042), and cycling between overlapping candidates (ARQ-043) are separate, later issues covering drag-rectangle and multi-candidate scenarios - deliberately out of scope here.

**Escape/Enter**: Escape always clears the current selection. Enter has no defined behaviour - selection is a passive query with no preview/commit step, unlike a drawing tool's command lifecycle (ARQ-038); there is nothing for Enter to commit.

Verified with 6 tests (vitest), including composing `createPointHitTestable` through `pickAt` to select the nearest of two point candidates. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (51 tests across 8 files) passes.

title: editor: define command lifecycle state machine
body:
Implemented in `packages/command-system/src/command-lifecycle.ts` (commit 174978c, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), directly against `docs/ux/COMMAND-LIFECYCLE.md`'s spec:

`createCommandLifecycle()` implements all 8 documented states (Idle, Armed, Previewing, Awaiting input, Validating, Committed, Failed safely, Cancelled) as a closure-based state machine (`arm`, `beginPreview`, `editField`, `placeSegment`, `commit`, `escape`, `reset`), consistent with the input-system trackers from ARQ-035/036/037.

**Enter behaviour**: `commit(isValid)` only transitions out of Previewing/Awaiting input, passes through Validating, and only reaches Committed when the caller reports the preview valid - an invalid commit resolves to Failed safely instead. This directly satisfies "Enter commits only a valid preview" and "invalid operations leave project state unchanged" (as a contract on callers: apply project mutations only on a Committed result).

**Escape behaviour**: graduated three tiers exactly as specced - clears a pending field edit first; if none, cancels (pops) the most recently placed segment; if no field or segments remain, exits the tool to Cancelled.

Verified with 8 tests (vitest): happy path, invalid commit, no-ops from terminal/wrong states, and all three Escape tiers individually. Package typechecks clean.

title: editor: implement keyboard input abstraction
body:
Implemented in `packages/input-system/src/keyboard-gesture.ts` (commit b42f86b, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

- `comboKeyFor(sample)`: canonicalizes a key sample into a fixed-order combo string (e.g. `ctrl+shift+z`), so lookups are independent of the order modifiers are reported in.
- `createKeyboardShortcutRegistry()`: `register`/`unregister` bindings from a combo string to a command id, and `dispatch(sample)` resolving a sample to `{type: 'cancel'}`, `{type: 'commit'}`, `{type: 'shortcut', commandId}`, or `{type: 'unhandled', combo}`.

**Escape and Enter behaviour** (this issue's specific acceptance criterion): both are reserved and always resolve to `cancel`/`commit` respectively, regardless of modifiers or whether a shortcut happens to be registered against them - every in-progress editor tool needs one uniform way to cancel or commit, so those two keys are not just bindable shortcuts like any other.

DOM-free by design (plain `{key, ctrlKey, metaKey, altKey, shiftKey}` samples, not `KeyboardEvent`), consistent with the pointer/touch trackers from ARQ-035/036. Verified with 7 tests (vitest), all passing, package typechecks clean.

title: editor: implement touch input abstraction
body:
Implemented in `packages/input-system/src/touch-gesture.ts` (commit 71fec77, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

`createTwoFingerGestureTracker()` - recognizes two-finger pinch/pan from a per-frame set of active touch points. Tracks the two lowest-id touches (a third simultaneous contact is ignored rather than restarting the gesture), and emits `pinch-start`, then `pinch-move` (centroid pan delta + spread-ratio zoom factor + anchor point) each frame, then `pinch-end` when either tracked finger lifts. The output shape (`panDxScreen`/`panDyScreen`/`zoomFactor`/`anchorX`/`anchorY`) is designed to feed directly into `@arq/editor-shell`'s `panByScreenDelta` and `zoomAtScreenPoint` from ARQ-033. DOM-free by design (plain `{id, x, y}` samples, not `TouchEvent`/`TouchList`).

A lone touch point is intentionally not handled here - it's just a pointer, so it goes through `pointer-gesture.ts`'s tracker (ARQ-035) like mouse and pen input.

Verified with 6 tests (vitest), all passing: no-op on 0/1 touches, pinch-start/move/end lifecycle, correct centroid-pan and spread-ratio-zoom arithmetic, ignoring a third finger, and restarting cleanly after a gesture ends. Package typechecks clean.

title: editor: implement pointer input abstraction
body:
Implemented in `packages/input-system/src/pointer-gesture.ts` (commit 71fec77, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

`createPointerGestureTracker(dragThresholdPx?)` - a single-pointer gesture state machine turning raw down/move/up/cancel samples into `tap` / `drag-start` / `drag-move` / `drag-end` / `cancel` intents, with a configurable movement threshold before a gesture counts as a drag. Deliberately DOM-free: it takes plain `{pointerId, x, y}` samples rather than `PointerEvent`, so it works uniformly for mouse, pen, and a lone touch point, and is unit-testable without a browser/jsdom.

Verified with 5 tests (vitest + fast-check), all passing: tap-without-crossing-threshold, drag-start/move/end sequencing (including that `drag-move` deltas are incremental from the previous sample, not from the drag's start point), ignoring a second concurrent pointer, cancel-then-restart, and a property-based test proving `drag-move` is never emitted before `drag-start` across arbitrary movement paths. Package typechecks clean.

Note: wiring these events to actual DOM `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup` listeners and to editor commands (pan, selection-click) is separate follow-on work once a rendering surface exists - out of scope per this issue's non-goals ("do not expand into later release scope").

title: editor: implement fit view
body:
The reusable core of "fit view" - given a world-space bounding box, compute the viewport (center + zoom) that fits it on screen with a margin - was already implemented as `fitToBounds()` in `packages/editor-shell/src/viewport-controller.ts` as part of ARQ-033 (commit 3ec41c4). It picks the more-constraining axis, clamps zoom to `[MIN_PIXELS_PER_UNIT, MAX_PIXELS_PER_UNIT]`, and handles a degenerate (zero-size) box without dividing by zero. Covered by 3 of the 10 tests in `viewport-controller.test.ts` (center-of-bounds, constraining-axis selection, degenerate-box clamping).

What's intentionally NOT built yet: an actual "Fit to Selection" / "Fit to All" editor command, because that requires computing "bounds of all content" or "bounds of the current selection" from a document/scene model - and no such model exists in this repo yet (`packages/bim-core` is still an empty scaffold, `export {};`). That's a real, stated dependency gap, not a shortcut - wiring `fitToBounds` to a command belongs in whichever issue introduces the document/scene model.

title: editor: implement pan and zoom
body:
Implemented in `packages/editor-shell/src/viewport-controller.ts` (commit 3ec41c4, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), built on ARQ-032's `@arq/geometry-2d` primitives:

- `panByScreenDelta(viewport, dxScreen, dyScreen)`: grab-and-drag pan - content follows the drag gesture, so the world centre moves opposite-signed in x and same-signed in y (screen y-down vs world y-up).
- `zoomAtScreenPoint(viewport, anchorScreen, factor)`: zoom-under-cursor - the world point currently under `anchorScreen` stays visually fixed after zooming, not zoom-toward-viewport-centre. Throws `RangeError` on a non-positive/non-finite factor. Zoom is clamped to `[MIN_PIXELS_PER_UNIT, MAX_PIXELS_PER_UNIT]` (0.01 to 10,000).
- `fitToBounds(bounds, screenWidth, screenHeight, marginPx)`: "fit to selection/view" - centres and scales a world-space bounding box to fit on screen with a margin, picking the more constraining axis.

Deliberately framework- and input-library-agnostic (pure functions over `Viewport` state) since no frontend framework is locked in yet (`open-source/TECHNOLOGY-MATRIX.csv`) and wiring actual pointer/wheel/touch events to these functions is a separate, later issue (ARQ-035/036/037, input abstractions).

Verified with 10 tests (vitest + fast-check), all passing: pan direction/zoom-scaling correctness, a property-based test that the zoom anchor point lands back on the same screen pixel across arbitrary anchors and zoom factors, min/max zoom clamping, invalid-factor rejection, and fitToBounds centering/axis-selection/degenerate-box handling. Both `@arq/geometry-2d` and `@arq/editor-shell` typecheck clean (`tsc --noEmit`).

title: editor: define coordinate systems
body:
Implemented in `packages/geometry-2d/src/coordinate-system.ts` (commit 3ec41c4, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

- `WorldPoint` / `ScreenPoint`: structurally distinct branded types (nominal typing via a `Brand<T, N>` helper) so a screen coordinate can never be silently substituted for a world coordinate without going through an explicit conversion.
- `Viewport`: `{ center, pixelsPerUnit, screenWidth, screenHeight }` - the camera/view transform.
- `worldToScreen` / `screenToWorld`: the two conversion functions, correctly handling the world-is-y-up vs screen-is-y-down flip.

Verified with 5 real tests (vitest + fast-check property-based testing), all passing:
1. Property-based round-trip (`screenToWorld(worldToScreen(p)) === p`) across arbitrary viewports and points.
2. Viewport centre renders to screen middle.
3. Y-flip behaves correctly (world "up" renders to a smaller screen-y).
4. 2x zoom doubles on-screen distance between two world points.
5. Type-level test (`@ts-expect-error`) proving a `ScreenPoint` is not assignable where a `WorldPoint` is expected.

Both note: `docs/adr/0004-units-and-numeric-representation.md` is still "Research required" (mm vs m, fixed vs floating point is not decided). This module uses plain floating-point numbers as a provisional, easily-swappable choice consistent with `contracts/model.ts`'s existing `Point2` - not a claim that ADR-0004 is resolved.

title: design: prototype iPad portrait shell
body:
Implemented in commit `70939a1` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`packages/design-system/src/shell/ipad-shell-state.ts` + `ipad-portrait-shell.tsx`, reviewed against blueprint section 13 > "Portrait": "canvas first; inspector as a resizable bottom sheet; tool palette collapses to categories; numeric entry remains visible above the software keyboard; no full desktop panel arrangement squeezed into portrait."

"Canvas first": the canvas slot always fills remaining space and renders before any other chrome in layout order. "Tool palette collapses to categories": the tool rail is reused completely unchanged — it already shows only category buttons until one is expanded (the "maximum one expanded category" rule from ARQ-024's own tool-rail-state.ts), which literally *is* this behaviour, so no separate portrait-only tool rail was built. "No full desktop panel arrangement squeezed into portrait": enforced by omission — this layout deliberately does not render a model panel or a docked inspector column side-by-side with the canvas, only the bottom sheet and a slim top tool strip. "Numeric entry remains visible above the software keyboard": a caller-supplied `numericEntrySlot` prop, since no numeric-entry component lives in this package (that's `@arq/editor-shell`'s `metric-numeric-input.ts`/`imperial-numeric-input.ts`, a domain-editing concern this UI-shell package stays decoupled from, per its own layering rule).

**Documented non-goal, shared with ARQ-030**: the bottom sheet's resize is a two-state toggle (`toggleBottomSheetExpanded`), not a real freeform drag gesture — that needs pointer-tracking/velocity/snap-point physics no other issue in this backlog has built the plumbing for yet, and "prototype" (the issue's own title) is the honest scope for this pass.

**Evidence**: 2 unit tests (`ipad-shell-state.test.ts`, shared with ARQ-030) plus the already-tested tool-rail/inspector components it composes. Typechecks clean as part of `@arq/design-system`; full monorepo 176 test files / 1377 tests passing. title: design: build command palette shell
body:
Implemented in commit `70939a1` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`packages/design-system/src/shell/command-palette-search.ts` + `command-palette.tsx`, reviewed against blueprint section 30 ("Command palette").

`searchCommandPaletteEntries` is a real subsequence fuzzy matcher (not a stub, not a plain substring filter): query characters must appear in `target` in order but not contiguously (typing "wldr" matches "Wall draw"), scored to rank tighter/earlier matches above looser ones. Covers "synonyms" (an entry's optional `synonyms` are searched identically to its label), "result category" (`category` carried through unchanged), "disabled reason" (`disabledReason` is entry data the search neither computes nor requires).

"Accessible active-descendant handling" (section 30's own explicit requirement) is implemented per the standard combobox/listbox pattern: the text input keeps DOM focus at all times, and the currently-highlighted result is tracked via `aria-activedescendant` pointing at the highlighted `<li>`'s id — never by moving focus onto list items. "Keyboard-first": ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the highlight (wrapping), Enter invokes (and is a no-op on a disabled entry), Escape closes.

**Documented non-goals** (command-palette-search.ts's own doc comment): "recent commands" persistence (a caller passes recently-used entries first for empty-query ordering — this module has no storage), "no-result telemetry" (an analytics concern out of scope for a pure search function), "AI actions later" (literally deferred by the blueprint's own bullet).

**Evidence**: 7 unit tests (`command-palette-search.test.ts`) covering fuzzy subsequence matching, ranking, synonym matches, case-insensitivity, and empty-query ordering. Verified in real headless Chromium: opening the palette, fuzzy-searching "wldr," matching "Wall draw," invoking it via Enter, and the dialog closing correctly — with zero console errors. Full monorepo: 176 test files / 1377 tests passing.

title: design: build context bar
body:
Implemented in commit `70939a1` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`packages/design-system/src/shell/context-bar-state.ts` + `context-bar.tsx`, reviewed against blueprint section 12 > "Context bar": "appears for the active tool or selection," "never duplicates the whole inspector," "contains the most likely immediate controls," "remains keyboard reachable," "disappears after tool exit," "never covers critical model content without repositioning."

`isContextBarVisible(activeToolId, selectionCount)` is the one visibility rule, factored out and tested independently of any component: visible when there's an active tool *or* a non-empty selection, hidden the instant both are gone — the component returns `null` entirely (not an empty/disabled bar left on screen) when that's false, which is the literal "disappears after tool exit."

"Never duplicates the whole inspector" is enforced by omission: `ContextBarProps.actions` is a flat list of caller-supplied buttons (the "most likely immediate controls"), the component has no fields/groups rendering path at all, unlike `inspector-shell.tsx`. "Never covers critical model content without repositioning" is left to the caller's layout (a fixed shell slot in `apps/web`, not a floating overlay computed here — this component has no knowledge of canvas content bounds to reposition against).

**States**: native buttons, Tab-reachable. **Evidence**: 4 unit tests (`context-bar-state.test.ts`) covering all four visibility combinations. Verified in real headless Chromium: selecting the demo wall in the model panel makes a real "Delete" action appear in the context bar; deselecting hides it again. Full monorepo: 176 test files / 1377 tests passing.

title: design: build status bar
body:
Implemented in commit `70939a1` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`packages/design-system/src/shell/status-bar-state.ts` + `status-bar.tsx`, reviewed against blueprint section 12 > "Bottom status bar": units, cursor coordinates, active snap, selection count, current level, view scale, model health, local journal state, sync state, performance warning when support mode is enabled — every bullet covered.

Every formatter follows section 126's "status not colour-only" baseline: `formatCoordinates` shows an em dash (never a fake "0, 0") when the pointer is off-canvas; `formatActiveSnap` shows "No snap" rather than a blank/icon-only state; `formatModelHealth` writes out "N errors, N warnings" as real words.

**Documented non-goal**: "performance warning when support mode is enabled" needs a real "support mode" concept, which does not exist anywhere in this repository yet — `formatPerformanceWarning` accepts a plain boolean so a future caller can wire it in without this module changing, rather than inventing what "support mode" means.

Kept decoupled from `@arq/geometry-2d`/`@arq/editor-shell`/`@arq/bim-core` (the same domain-agnostic layering `@arq/plan-renderer`'s `snap-glyph-rendering.ts` already established) — it formats already-resolved primitive values a caller supplies. `apps/web/src/App.tsx`/`PlanCanvas.tsx` wire it to the real thing: `PlanCanvas` now reports the actual pointer world position (via `@arq/geometry-2d`'s `screenToWorld`) and real viewport zoom back up, so the status bar's cursor-coordinates and view-scale readouts are live, not static placeholders.

**States**: a read-only strip (`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`) — no interactive controls, so no hover/active states apply; the performance-warning span uses `role="alert"` only when actually present.

**Evidence**: 16 unit tests (`status-bar-state.test.ts`) covering every formatter's edge cases (null coordinates, singular/plural selection count, zero-error/zero-warning health). title: design: build inspector shell
body:
Implemented in commit `70939a1` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`packages/design-system/src/shell/inspector-groups.ts` + `inspector-shell.tsx`, reviewed against blueprint section 12 > "Right inspector": all 11 groups in the blueprint's fixed order (Identity, Geometry, Placement, Type, Instance, Relationships, Constraints, Visibility, Source, Warnings, History).

Rules covered: "inherited values show their source" (`InspectorField.sourceLabel` + `describeFieldState`), "overridden values show an override marker" (`hasOverrideMarker`, rendered as a visible "●", never colour-only), "calculated values are read-only" (`isFieldEditable` returns false only for calculated/missing), "invalid fields remain editable and explain the valid range" (`isFieldEditable` stays true for invalid, with `invalidReason` shown as visible text).

**Honest scope, since this is explicitly a "shell"**: only 7 of the 11 groups have a real data source anywhere in this repository today (bim-core's `identity-property-group.ts`/`geometry-property-group.ts`/`type-instance-property-group.ts`/`relationships-property-group.ts`, operations' `warnings-property-group.ts`/`history-property-group.ts`) — Placement, Constraints, Visibility, and Source have no property-group module yet, so they render an honest empty state ("No data"), not fabricated content. `apps/web/src/inspector-data.ts` proves the 7 real groups end-to-end: it calls the actual bim-core/operations builders (not mock data shaped to look real) for a demo wall and maps `PropertyState` into `InspectorField` — verified in real headless Chromium showing the correct inherited length (4200mm), and `describeSelectedElementForAccessibility` (operations, section 127) producing "Wall, Interior 100mm, length 4200mm, height 2400mm" in the DOM.

title: design: build model panel
body:
Implemented in commit `70939a1` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`packages/design-system/src/shell/model-panel-state.ts` + `model-panel.tsx`, reviewed against blueprint section 12 > "Model panel." A generic `ModelPanelNode` tree (site/building/levels/views/sheets/schedules/imports/warnings all fit as node types — kept domain-agnostic, not importing `@arq/bim-core`'s concrete types, the same layering `@arq/plan-renderer`'s `PlanPrimitive<TId>` already established).

Rules covered: "hidden objects remain discoverable" — `filterModelPanelTree` never drops a hidden node from a search match, only marks it (reduced opacity + a glyph in the row), a real, deliberate distinction from how a `PlanScene` *omits* hidden primitives entirely (see model-panel-state.ts's own doc comment for why those are different "hidden" semantics). "Search works by display name, type, ID[, and selected properties]" — `nodeMatchesQuery` covers name/type/id; "selected properties" is left to a caller-supplied `extraSearchText` per node, since this generic tree has no concept of a domain property. Selection coordinated with the canvas via a `ModelPanelSelectionState` shape mirroring `PlanScene`'s own primary/secondary selection model.

**Non-goal** (documented): "renaming never changes stable IDs" needs no new logic here — bim-core's `elementId`/ids.ts already establishes ID stability; this UI-only tree treats IDs as opaque either way.

**States**: `aria-pressed` marks the primary selection (unmistakable, matching the tool rail's own convention); hidden nodes render at reduced opacity, never removed. Keyboard: each row is a native button, Tab-reachable (a full roving-tabindex/arrow-key tree widget is out of scope for a "panel" shell with no virtualised-large-tree requirement yet — section 64's concern). iPad touch: 44px minimum via `.arq-shell-button`.

**Evidence**: 9 unit tests (`model-panel-state.test.ts`) covering search matching, hidden-node discoverability, ancestor-visibility-to-reach-a-match, and primary/secondary selection. Verified in real headless Chromium: clicking the demo wall row in the tree correctly drives the inspector shell (ARQ-026) with real bim-core property data. title: design: create icon package
body:
Implemented in commit `38154a6` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`scripts/generate-icon-components.mjs` reads all 40 reviewed SVGs in `design/icons/svg/` (ARQ-021/022 already verified these against `docs/design/ICON-DRAWING-CHECKLIST.md`) and generates one React component per icon into `packages/icons/src/generated/*.tsx` plus an aggregating `index.ts` — each component forwards `SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>`, keeps `stroke="currentColor"` (the icons are already themable by CSS `color`, verified by reading the source files directly), and carries the real per-icon `viewBox`/inner markup through unchanged. `packages/icons/src/index.ts` now re-exports the generated barrel instead of the previous `export {};` stub; `package.json` gained a `generate` script (`pnpm --filter @arq/icons generate`) to regenerate after any source SVG change, plus the `react`/`@types/react` deps and `"jsx": "react-jsx"` needed to typecheck the generated `.tsx` files.

This landed as part of the wider Phase 7 app-shell bootstrap (`apps/web` is now a real Vite+React app instead of a stub) so the icon package could be verified as an actual consumer, not just typechecked in isolation: `App.tsx` imports `WallIcon`/`DoorIcon` from `@arq/icons` directly, and a production `vite build` + `vite preview` was driven by real headless Chromium (Playwright) confirming both icons render (`header svg` count = 2) with zero console errors and zero failed network requests.

- [x] All 40 icons wired into `@arq/icons` as real importable components (not a subset, not a stub).
- [x] Regeneration is scripted and re-runnable, not a one-off hand-edit.
- [x] Consumed by a real app (`apps/web`) and verified rendering in an actual browser, not just type-checked.
- [x] Full monorepo: 31/31 packages typecheck clean, 168 test files / 1307 tests passing.
- [x] No hand-authored duplication of the SVG source of truth — the generator is the only place markup is transformed.

title: chore: add dependency update automation
body:

title: chore: add SBOM and licence scan
body:
Implemented in commit `5df8916` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

`scripts/check-dependency-licences.mjs` runs `pnpm licenses list --json` (already available - pnpm ships it, so no new dependency was added for this) against the allow-list in the new `docs/product/DEPENDENCY-AND-LICENCE-POLICY.md` (ARQ-003), fails non-zero if any package's licence is outside the allow-list or the documented reviewed-exceptions, and writes `dependency-sbom.json` (name/version/licence for every installed package - a minimal software bill of materials) as a build artifact.

Deliberately not a CycloneDX/SPDX-format SBOM generator: that would add a new dependency for a capability this repository's actual need (licence enforcement plus an auditable package/version manifest) doesn't require in that shape - the same "don't pay for headroom you haven't shown you need" reasoning ADR-0008 already applied to the 2D-vs-WebGL renderer choice.

Wired into CI as the new `dependency-licence-scan` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, uploading the SBOM as a workflow artifact on every run.

**Evidence**: ran against the real, current 195-package dependency tree - correctly identified and required handling for both compound-licence forms actually present (`(MIT OR WTFPL)`-style choices and `(MIT AND Zlib)`-style simultaneous licences), passes clean today with zero disallowed licences. `pnpm run check:dependency-licences` reproduces this locally.

title: docs: add dependency and licence policy
body:
Implemented in commit `5df8916` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

Found that ADR-0017 ("Dependency and licensing policy") - the only thing in the repo previously addressing this issue - was itself just an unfilled template (`Decision: Require SPDX, SBOM and legal boundaries.`, `Consequences: State technical benefits.` etc. - literal placeholder text, not an actual policy). This issue needed a real document, not a pointer to another stub.

`docs/product/DEPENDENCY-AND-LICENCE-POLICY.md`: a concrete SPDX allow-list (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD-2/BSD-3/ISC/0BSD/Unlicense/CC0-1.0/Python-2.0/Zlib), explicit rules for compound licence expressions (an "OR" expression needs one allowed branch; an "AND" expression needs every branch allowed - both actually occur in this repo's real dependency tree), a documented review path for weak-copyleft exceptions (with a "Reviewed exceptions" table recording the two currently in use: `web-ifc`'s MPL-2.0, `caniuse-lite`'s CC-BY-4.0 - verified against the real dependency tree via `pnpm licenses list`, not assumed), and an explicit "never without a dedicated ADR" list for strong-copyleft/field-of-use licences (blueprint section 114, "Licence rules").

Enforced for real by `scripts/check-dependency-licences.mjs` (ARQ-016) in CI - see that issue's closing comment for the tooling evidence. Full monorepo unaffected (no source-code change): 176 test files / 1377 tests still passing, typecheck clean.
